title: Nature as the basis of the economy
context: Evaluate the following statements on embedding the economy in nature:
statements: Nature's services are indispensable for the production of goods and services.
Dependence on nature mainly concerns tourism; laptop production and insurance can largely be explained without a natural basis.
Nature's services form the foundation of our economic system, not only of individual industries.
Economic activities can be modelled as a largely autonomous process that remains independent of social decisions about resource use.
Technical goods such as laptops and everyday food also presuppose nature's services in production.
tactical_explanations:
Goods and services do not arise in a vacuum. Fields, materials, environmental services and landscape foundations support production and service offerings. Anyone who treats nature as mere scenery overlooks exactly this indispensability for both — products and services.

The statement is true.

Explaining dependence on nature through tourism alone is too narrow. Food and laptops stand for the goods side, tourism and insurance for services; all need nature's services. Treating laptop production and insurance as nature-free misses the embedding of the economy in the biophysical sphere.

The statement is false.

Nature does not only supply raw materials for individual products, but the foundation on which the economic system as a whole runs. Without the biophysical sphere there is no economy in this sense — industry differences do not change that.

The statement is true.

Autonomy sounds like a closed loop of prices and quantities. But the economy is an expression of social decisions about resource use, distribution and justice. Anyone who brackets out resource use separates off the decision level that belongs to embedding.

The statement is false.

Everyday food and technical hardware both rest on nature's services, not only agriculture. The twin example prevents the mistaken assumption that only fields and forests hang on the Earth system while electronics arise free of nature.

The statement is true.

title: Who carries out economic activities
context: Evaluate the following statements on who carries out economic activities:
statements: Economic activities are carried out primarily by privately run enterprises; households and the public sector count more as marginal actors.
Households and communities carry out economic activities.
In this embedding, the public sector includes the state and NGOs.
Goods and services arise mainly with the state; private enterprises play a secondary role.
Privately run enterprises, the public sector, and households and communities carry out economic activities.
tactical_explanations:
Three carriers carry out economic activities: privately run enterprises, the public sector, and households and communities. Treating households and the public sector as marginal actors dilutes exactly this three-way split.

The statement is false.

Households do not merely sit on the sidelines as buyers. Together with communities they belong among the actors who carry out economic activities — provisioning, working, demanding and communal economic activity sit inside the economy.

The statement is true.

The public sector comprises the state and NGOs. Later NGOs also appear in civil society; that does not change the assignment in the simplified embedding. For this statement, the parenthesis state and NGOs is enough.

The statement is true.

Enterprises count among the carriers alongside households and the public sector. The state alone does not create all goods and services; that arises with several actor groups at once.

The statement is false.

The guideline is the three-way split: privately run enterprises, public sector, households and communities. All three carry out activities, take inputs from nature and return outputs.

The statement is true.

title: Inputs from the Earth system and outputs back
context: Evaluate the following statements on inputs and outputs between the economy and the Earth system:
statements: The economy takes inputs such as natural resources and environmental services from the Earth system.
Pollination of food plants is an example of an output of the economy into nature.
Climate gases and waste are examples of outputs returned to the Earth system.
The biophysical sphere denotes the Earth system into which the economy's outputs flow back.
Economic activities take inputs from nature but return little waste or emissions as long as production is organised efficiently.
tactical_explanations:
Metabolism begins in nature. Natural resources and environmental services come as inputs from the Earth system into the economy. Without this inflow, goods and services would not exist in the familiar form.

The statement is true.

Reading pollination as an output reverses the arrow. Pollination of food plants is an environmental service — hence an input. Outputs in the other direction include climate gases and waste. Anyone who declares the bee an emission of the economy confuses extraction and return.

The statement is false.

What the economy does not bind or store comes back as output. Climate gases and waste are typical returns to the Earth system. Emission and residual material belong to the same return flow, not to the inputs.

The statement is true.

Earth system and biophysical sphere stand as the same target of the outputs. The economy is framed by this sphere, not by empty space. Anyone who swaps it for the social environment confuses environment with institutions and norms.

The statement is true.

Efficiency reduces quantities but does not erase the return flow. Waste, emissions and other environmental damage flow back into nature; all economic activities have impacts on nature. A pure extraction process without return is not envisaged.

The statement is false.

title: Atmospheric greenhouse gases
context: Evaluate the following statements on greenhouse gases in the atmosphere:
statements: Water vapour, carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide and ozone are among the most important atmospheric greenhouse gases.
Nitrous oxide is also called laughing gas.
Greenhouse gases let most of the heat radiated from the Earth's surface pass unhindered into space and retain only negligible residual heat.
These gases form a kind of insulating layer in the atmosphere that retains part of the radiated heat.
For the greenhouse effect it is practically enough to consider carbon dioxide; methane and ozone play no comparable role in the atmosphere.
tactical_explanations:
Carbon dioxide alone would be an impermissible shortening. Water vapour, carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide and ozone stand as the most important atmospheric greenhouse gases. The insulating layer arises from this mixture, not from a single molecule.

The statement is true.

Laughing gas is the everyday name for nitrous oxide (N₂O). The double designation refers to the same gas in the greenhouse list, not to an extra beside N₂O.

The statement is true.

Insulating layer means retention, not free passage. The gases retain part of the heat radiated from the Earth's surface. The claim that heat largely goes unhindered into space erases exactly this insulating effect.

The statement is false.

Heat radiates from the surface; the gas layer holds part of it. Neither complete blockage nor complete loss describes the mechanism; exactly the retained part is the core.

The statement is true.

Methane and ozone stand in the same enumeration as carbon dioxide, plus water vapour and nitrous oxide. Treating only CO₂ as a practically relevant greenhouse gas is incompatible with this list.

The statement is false.

title: Human activities and climate change
context: Evaluate the following statements on causes of rising greenhouse gas concentrations:
statements: Burning fossil fuels drives the concentrations; deforestation of forests contributes little to this.
Agricultural intensification contributes to the rise in concentrations of these gases.
Rising concentrations of these gases lower the global average temperature.
The rise in global average temperature accelerates climate change.
Deforestation of forests is among the human activities that cause concentrations to rise.
tactical_explanations:
Three human activities stand side by side: burning fossil fuels, deforestation of forests and agricultural intensification. Treating deforestation as barely relevant removes one of the three drivers of concentrations.

The statement is false.

More intensive agriculture is a driver of its own alongside fossil combustion and deforestation. It belongs among the human activities that raise greenhouse gas concentrations.

The statement is true.

The causal chain runs from higher concentrations to a higher, not a lower, average temperature. The insulating layer holds more heat; claiming cooling reverses the effect.

The statement is false.

Temperature rise and accelerated climate change follow the higher concentrations. More retained heat raises the global average temperature; this rise accelerates climate change.

The statement is true.

Clearing forests stands in the list of causes alongside fossil combustion and intensification of agriculture. Deforestation is human activity that causes greenhouse gas concentrations to rise.

The statement is true.

title: Dependence of selected industries
context: Evaluate the following statements on the dependence of economic activities on nature:
statements: All economic activities have impacts on nature.
Above all resource-related industries burden nature; many service activities count as largely environmentally neutral.
Fisheries, agriculture and forestry, and tourism depend to a high degree on natural resources and intact ecosystems.
Some economic activities also depend directly on nature.
Long-term existence and productivity of these particularly dependent areas hinge on conservation and sustainable use of the natural foundations.
tactical_explanations:
The line of impact applies without industry exception. All economic activities have impacts on nature, even if strength and form differ. Even those who do not fish or fell timber return outputs.

The statement is true.

Environmental neutrality for large parts of the economy does not stand. All activities affect nature; in addition some depend on it directly. The distinction concerns dependence, not the claim that whole sectors leave barely any traces.

The statement is false.

The four-item list marks high dependence: fisheries, agriculture and forestry, and tourism. They need available natural resources and intact ecosystems to a particular degree.

The statement is true.

All have impact; direct dependence especially concerns the resource-related areas. The two do not exclude each other: some activities also depend directly on nature.

The statement is true.

Conservation and sustainable use are the condition of continuation. Long-term existence and productivity of the particularly dependent areas hinge on the natural foundations; anyone who destroys them undermines catch, harvest, timber and tourist landscape.

The statement is true.

title: The economy in the social environment
context: Evaluate the following statements on embedding the economy in society:
statements: The economy is embedded in a social environment.
The state, enterprises, civil society and social groups shape this environment.
Economic processes can essentially be explained as technical procedures; social and political negotiation plays a secondary role.
Changed consumption habits and social values barely feed back onto the economy.
The processes in society and nature feed back onto the economy.
tactical_explanations:
The economy sits in a social environment that actors shape, and at the same time in the biophysical sphere. Prices and quantities do not float free above the state, norms and groups.

The statement is true.

Four shapers: state, enterprises, civil society and social groups. The environment arises in interplay, not through a single sovereign alone.

The statement is true.

Economic processes are also the result of social and political negotiation processes. Purely technical procedures without society would strike the state, lobbying, civil society, purchasing decisions and protests out of the explanation.

The statement is false.

Feedback from society runs among other things through changed consumption habits and social values. Anyone who denies them allows only nature costs and overlooks the social feedback.

The statement is false.

Two directions belong together: environmental destruction creates costs for the economy; society shifts demand and values. Both feed back onto the economy.

The statement is true.

title: Central role of the state
context: Evaluate the following statements on the role of the state:
statements: For the economy the state remains mainly a spectator; other actors set the framework conditions.
The state enacts laws, enforces regulations and creates economic framework conditions.
Tax policy and environmental requirements are examples of such framework conditions.
Environmental requirements arise mainly within enterprises themselves; the state barely intervenes here.
The state has a central role by, among other things, setting legal and regulatory frameworks.
tactical_explanations:
The state enacts laws, enforces regulations and creates economic framework conditions, for example through tax policy or environmental requirements. Making it a spectator contradicts this central role.

The statement is false.

Three state tasks stand together: enacting laws, enforcing regulations, creating economic framework conditions. The frame within which enterprises then act arises here politically.

The statement is true.

Tax policy and environmental requirements show that the state steers through levies and requirements, not only through criminal law in the narrow sense. Both belong to the toolkit of framework conditions.

The statement is true.

Environmental requirements are state framework conditions, not a private norm of enterprises. Enterprises can additionally self-regulate and launch CSR, but that does not replace the state requirement.

The statement is false.

Central means: without this actor the legal and regulatory frame is missing. Enacting, enforcing and creating conditions together form the described role.

The statement is true.

title: Enterprises between framework and influence
context: Evaluate the following statements on how enterprises act in the social environment:
statements: Enterprises act within the state's framework conditions.
Enterprises can barely influence framework conditions because lobbying has little effect in practice.
Self-regulation and corporate social responsibility initiatives are ways through which enterprises actively help shape framework conditions.
Lobbying counts as a form of active influence by enterprises on framework conditions.
Corporate social responsibility can largely replace state laws if enterprises take enough responsibility.
tactical_explanations:
First the framework, then action within it. Enterprises act within the conditions the state sets. That does not rule out later co-shaping, but names the starting point: they do not stand in a law-free space.

The statement is true.

They still actively influence the framework. Lobbying, self-regulation and CSR initiatives stand as paths of this influence. Dismissing lobbying as ineffective claims a powerlessness that does not match the embedding.

The statement is false.

Self-regulation and CSR come alongside lobbying. Both are forms in which enterprises do not only accept the framework but help form it — as real practice beside state regulation, not as a substitute for all laws.

The statement is true.

Lobbying denotes the active influence of enterprises on framework conditions while they also act within those frameworks. Being bound and co-shaping exist side by side.

The statement is true.

CSR supplements state law; it does not replace it. The state continues to enact laws and environmental requirements; enterprises can additionally initiate responsibility. Far-reaching substitution would erase the central role of the state.

The statement is false.

title: Civil society as a critical instance
context: Evaluate the following statements on civil society:
statements: Civil society comprises NGOs, associations, science and the media.
Civil society tends to affirm economic action rather than to address grievances.
Expectations of sustainable business are formulated mainly by the state; civil society remains reserved here.
Civil society functions as a critical instance that questions economic action.
It formulates societal expectations of sustainable and ethical business.
tactical_explanations:
Four building blocks fill the concept: NGOs, associations, science and the media. Civil society is thus broader than a single protest group or a single authority.

The statement is true.

Critical instance means questioning, not nodding along. Civil society addresses grievances; it formulates expectations of sustainable and ethical business. Uncritical affirmation contradicts this functional description.

The statement is false.

Expectations of sustainable and ethical business are formulated precisely by civil society. The state sets the frame, enterprises lobby, civil society brings societal claims into speech. Reserve would be the opposite of this role.

The statement is false.

Questioning is the lead verb: economic action is not taken as given but examined. Exactly that makes civil society the critical instance beside state and enterprises.

The statement is true.

Sustainable and ethical stand as the content of the expectations. Civil society brings these claims into the negotiation from which economic processes also emerge.

The statement is true.

title: Consumers, workers and co-shaping
context: Evaluate the following statements on individual and collective actors:
statements: Above all enterprises and the state shape economic structures; consumers have only little influence on them.
Purchasing decisions can help shape economic structures and norms.
Labour mobility and protests are behaviours with which actors help shape economic structures.
Workers have only little influence on economic norms.
Consumers and workers belong among the actors who contribute through behaviour and decisions.
tactical_explanations:
Individual and collective actors stand beside state, enterprises and civil society. Consumers help shape structures and norms through purchasing decisions, labour mobility or protests. Little influence contradicts this co-shaping.

The statement is false.

Purchasing decisions belong to co-shaping economic structures and norms, not only to private need satisfaction. What households choose or avoid shifts which offers endure.

The statement is true.

Labour mobility and protests complement buying. Anyone who changes jobs or publicly objects acts in the same logic on structures and norms.

The statement is true.

Workers stand with consumers. Their behaviour, including mobility and protest, counts as co-shaping. Dismissing influence as slight strikes this actor group out of the embedding.

The statement is false.

The dual role of consumption and work covers everyday life and employment. Both groups belong among the actors who, through behaviour and decisions, help shape economic structures and norms.

The statement is true.

title: Direct and indirect costs of environmental destruction
context: Evaluate the following statements on economic costs of environmental destruction:
statements: Environmental destruction causes substantial costs for the economy.
Direct consequences show mainly in image losses, less in infrastructure or production.
Destroyed infrastructure through extreme weather events, production outages and rising insurance claims are direct consequences.
Crop failures, higher health costs and productivity losses count among direct infrastructure damages.
The costs can be divided into direct and indirect damages.
tactical_explanations:
Feedback from nature destruction is expensive. Substantial costs for the economy split into direct and indirect damages: extreme weather hits infrastructure, outages hit production, claims hit insurers; later come crops, health and productivity.

The statement is true.

Direct consequences are destroyed infrastructure through extreme weather, production outages and rising insurance claims. Treating image losses as a typical direct consequence pulls the cost concept into a marketing theme that is not meant here.

The statement is false.

Three direct examples stand in a row: infrastructure after extreme weather, halted production, higher insurance claims. They hit assets, output and risk transfer immediately.

The statement is true.

Crop failures, higher health costs and productivity losses stand under the indirect impacts, not under the direct infrastructure damages. Swapping the assignment mixes the two cost baskets.

The statement is false.

First the distinction direct versus indirect, then the examples. Without this bipartition only an unsorted damage cloud would remain.

The statement is true.

title: Long-term challenges and adaptation
context: Evaluate the following statements on long-term climate impacts and adaptation:
statements: Degradation of ecosystems and climate-related migration intensify economic challenges in the long run.
Rising investment risks and disruptions of global supply chains belong among these long-term intensifications.
Adaptation to climate impacts requires only small investments because ecosystems largely regenerate themselves.
Resilient infrastructures, renewable energies and sustainable economic models are central investment fields of adaptation.
Society affects the economy mainly through tax laws, barely through consumption habits.
tactical_explanations:
In the long run the burden list hardens beyond the immediate storm damage. Degradation of ecosystems and climate-related migration stand beside investment risks and supply-chain disruptions as intensification of economic challenges.

The statement is true.

Investment risk and the global supply chain close the long-term enumeration. Disruptions hit networked production; rising investment risks make projects more expensive or shift them.

The statement is true.

Adaptation demands substantial investments in resilient infrastructures, renewable energies and sustainable economic models. Far-reaching self-healing without resource use does not stand; economic stability is to be secured through exactly these investments.

The statement is false.

Three investment fields secure economic stability in this logic: resilient infrastructures, renewable energies, sustainable economic models. They are the answer to climate impacts.

The statement is true.

Consumption habits and social values are a named societal feedback channel. Tax policy belongs to state framework-setting but does not replace this societal effect.

The statement is false.

title: Ecosystems as protection against disasters
context: Evaluate the following statements on healthy ecosystems and natural hazards:
statements: Healthy ecosystems barely serve as protection against natural disasters; technical structures are decisive.
Forests can prevent or dampen floods by storing rainwater and releasing it again in a controlled way.
In high alpine regions forests can catch avalanches as natural barriers and protect settlements, transport routes and infrastructures.
Wetlands tend to amplify floods because they take up and retain water only to a limited extent.
These ecological functions reduce direct damages to infrastructure and property and promote regeneration after disasters.
tactical_explanations:
Healthy ecosystems serve as natural protection against natural disasters; forests, alpine barriers and wetlands are examples. That does not exclude technical structures, but striking ecosystems out of protection overlooks storing rainwater, avalanche barriers and sponge effect.

The statement is false.

Storing and releasing again in a controlled way is the flood mechanism of the forest. Thereby floods can be prevented or dampened — temporal stretching of the water, not complete disappearance of precipitation.

The statement is true.

High alpine adds the avalanche to the water store. Forests act as natural barriers, catch avalanches and protect settlements, transport routes and infrastructures.

The statement is true.

Sponge, not amplifier: wetlands take up floodwater and retain it. Amplification would reverse this buffer function.

The statement is false.

Fewer direct damages to infrastructure and property plus better regeneration afterwards — that is the economic return of the ecological functions. Protection reduces direct costs in extreme weather and eases rebuilding.

The statement is true.

title: Biodiversity, resilience and innovation
context: Evaluate the following statements on species diversity and economic development:
statements: Species diversity in an ecosystem raises its resilience.
Biodiversity makes ecosystems more rigid so that they recover more slowly after disturbances.
By protecting biological diversity we contribute to the stability of natural systems, which strengthens the resilience of dependent communities.
Biodiversity is an important source of innovations in pharmacy, biotechnology and agriculture.
Many valuable compounds and genetic resources come rather from laboratories than from nature and play a secondary role for new products.
tactical_explanations:
Species diversity and resilience run in parallel. A diverse ecosystem can adapt to changes and recover faster after disturbances. Higher biodiversity means more, not less, resilience.

The statement is true.

Recover faster, not slower: biodiversity enables adaptation and quicker regeneration. Rigidity and delayed recovery claim the opposite of the mechanism.

The statement is false.

Two stages: first stability of natural systems through protection of biological diversity, then stronger resilience of the communities that depend on these ecosystems.

The statement is true.

Pharmacy, biotechnology and agriculture are innovation fields in which biodiversity is an important source: compounds and genetic resources from nature lead to new products and technologies.

The statement is true.

Many valuable compounds and genetic resources come from nature and lead to new products. Reversing origin and benefit contradicts both halves and underestimates the contribution to economic development.

The statement is false.

title: The economy as a social expression
context: Evaluate the following statements on the interplay of economy, society and nature:
statements: Economic activities take inputs from nature and return outputs such as waste and emissions to it.
Economic activities are embedded in social institutions, norms and political rules.
The economy can be understood as a largely autonomous process that remains independent of social decisions about resource use, distribution and justice.
A simplified representation of the economic cycle forgoes many details but still makes central connections visible.
Economic activities are carried out mainly by enterprises; households and the state play a secondary role.
tactical_explanations:
The material cycle runs in both directions: inputs from nature, outputs such as waste and emissions back. Anyone who only considers extraction overlooks the return side.

The statement is true.

Social institutions, norms and political rules enclose economic activities. The economy is thus not only metabolism with nature but also the rulebook of society.

The statement is true.

Not an autonomous process, but an expression of social decisions about resource use, distribution and justice. Autonomy would make exactly these decisions invisible.

The statement is false.

Simplification and informative power are not mutually exclusive. A deliberately simplified representation forgoes details and still clarifies the central connections between biophysical sphere, social environment and economic activities.

The statement is true.

Households, enterprises and the state jointly carry out economic activities. Naming only enterprises strikes out two of the three carriers.

The statement is false.

title: Needs in the future as well
context: Evaluate the following statements on the meaning of sustainability:
statements: Sustainability means that the joint system of economy and environment can also satisfy people's needs in the future.
A sustainable system refers mainly to the environment; economy and society remain outside.
Economic action counts as sustainable when it takes place within the biophysical limits of the planet without destroying the natural foundations of life.
An economic system that does not take these principles into account endangers mainly the environment, but barely its own stability.
Sustainable economic structures cover the needs of all people and at the same time promote social inclusion and social cohesion.
tactical_explanations:
Sustainability aims at the joint system of economy and environment. People's needs should still be fulfilable later. Without this temporal stretch, sustainability remains a label for today's production.

The statement is true.

Economy, society and environment form the system that can count as sustainable. A pure environmental formula without economy and society is too narrow; social inclusion and acting within planetary boundaries belong to it.

The statement is false.

Staying within biophysical limits and not destroying foundations of life is the operational condition. Sustainability ties to planetary boundaries, not to an arbitrary label.

The statement is true.

Ignored principles do not hit only forests or waters. The stability of the economic system and social welfare are also endangered. Narrowing to the environment alone is too tight.

The statement is false.

Needs of all people and social cohesion stand beside the ecological limit. Sustainability is threefold: biophysical limit, need coverage, social hold.

The statement is true.

title: Resources back into the cycle
context: Evaluate the following statements on resource extraction and sustainable economic structures:
statements: What matters is how resources are extracted, used and returned into cycles so that ecological load limits are not exceeded.
As soon as an enterprise makes a profit, its action counts as largely sustainable, regardless of environmental effects.
Economically successful action in the long run includes that enterprises and consumers take impacts on others and the environment into account.
Sustainable and resilient economic systems should promote people's well-being and at the same time preserve the health of ecosystems.
Ignoring interactions between nature and the economy accelerates the path to resilient systems.
tactical_explanations:
Extraction, use and return decide whether load limits hold. Anyone who takes raw materials and barely returns them drives exceedance forward. Designing the flows is the lever.

The statement is true.

Profit alone does not prove sustainability. A positive result can arise precisely because follow-on costs are shifted onto the environment or third parties. Sustainability couples to limits and impacts, not to the profit account alone.

The statement is false.

Long-term success requires responsible action: taking impacts on others and the environment into account. Enterprises and households both stand under that duty.

The statement is true.

Well-being and intact ecosystems are the twin goal. Resilience arises when both are thought together — and, not or.

The statement is true.

Blanking out interactions weakens systems. Recognising the coupling is a precondition for sustainable, resilient economy; ignorance is the opposite.

The statement is false.

title: Take, make, waste in production
context: Evaluate the following statements on linear economic activity:
statements: In many areas economic action still follows the linear principle of extracting raw materials, manufacturing products, consuming them and then disposing of them.
The possibility of reusing, repairing or recycling materials is usually used consistently in linear systems.
A linear resource flow leads to growing environmental burden, rising resource consumption and increasing pressure on planetary boundaries.
This way of doing business can destabilise central biophysical systems such as climate, biodiversity, land and water.
Linear economic activity mainly concerns the environment; economic stability and human well-being remain largely untouched by it.
tactical_explanations:
Take raw materials, manufacture, use, throw away: the linear pattern (take–make–waste). Extraction without sufficient return remains the normal case in many areas.

The statement is true.

Circular use is often neglected in the linear model, not used consistently. Reuse, repair and recycling would be the alternative but often remain unused.

The statement is false.

Growing burden, more consumption, more pressure on planetary boundaries: those are the consequences of the linear flow. Linearity is a driver of ecological exceedance.

The statement is true.

Climate, biodiversity, land and water are biophysical systems that are destabilised under linear pressure. Destabilisation hits the physical basis of the economy.

The statement is true.

Consequences do not stop at the environmental boundary. Climate crisis, biodiversity loss and overuse also endanger economic stability and human well-being.

The statement is false.

title: External costs of a furniture factory
context: Evaluate the following statements on external costs and short-term profit maximisation:
statements: For individual actors it often pays to maximise short-term profits and lower production costs while shifting follow-on costs onto others or onto future generations.
External costs do not arise with the enterprise or the consumers themselves, but are borne by society or through ecological damages.
Anyone who outsources emissions and social exploitation has thereby largely included the social costs in the product price.
Climate crisis, loss of biodiversity and overuse of natural resources endanger the environment, economic stability and human well-being.
Intensive extraction of natural resources without regard to ecological load limits already counts as overcome in most areas.
tactical_explanations:
Short-term profit maximisation and cost cutting often pay for individuals precisely because follow-on costs are externalised. That is the incentive logic behind external costs.

The statement is true.

External costs do not arise with the causer themselves, but are borne by society or through ecological damages — environmental destruction and social exploitation are typical examples.

The statement is true.

Outsourcing means externalising, not internalising. Anyone who shifts emissions and exploitation leaves follow-on costs precisely outside the product price. The social costs are then not included.

The statement is false.

The named consequences endanger not only the environment but also economic stability and human well-being. People and markets hang on the same systems.

The statement is true.

In many areas action still rests on intensive extraction without sufficient regard to load limits. Presenting it as largely overcome misses the finding.

The statement is false.

title: Cycle instead of disposal
context: Evaluate the following statements on the circular economy:
statements: In the circular economy waste is minimised and resources are kept in the economic cycle as long as possible.
Products, materials and raw materials are thereby reused, repaired or recycled.
The aim is to preserve the value of resources for as long as possible and thereby lower environmental burden as well as create economic advantages.
Circular economy means in essence using raw materials once and then largely disposing of them.
A sustainable economy must act within ecological limits and at the same time secure the well-being of all people.
tactical_explanations:
Minimising waste and keeping resources in the cycle as long as possible: that is the core of the circular economy versus linear disposal.

The statement is true.

Reusing, repairing or recycling keeps products, materials and raw materials in the economic cycle. Exactly these practices replace pure disposal logic.

The statement is true.

Preserving value as long as possible is meant to lower environmental burden and at the same time create economic advantages. Ecology and economy are not played off against each other here.

The statement is true.

Using once and largely disposing is the linear pattern, not the circular economy. The cycle keeps resources in the system; disposal ends private use, not the ecological load.

The statement is false.

A sustainable economy connects ecological limits with the well-being of all people. New models rely on circular economy, regenerative resource flows and social justice.

The statement is true.

title: Repair bonus and circular design
context: Evaluate the following statements on related concepts of the circular economy:
statements: Repair bonus, circular design, durable products and urban mining are concepts related to the circular economy.
Sharing models and durable designs count as ways to make economic growth less environmentally burdensome.
Remanufacturing, the reconditioning of used parts, can save raw materials, reduce emissions and at the same time create new economic opportunities.
Circular design aims rather at single-use products and stands against the idea of durable products.
The repair bonus belongs rather to linear disposal logic than to circular considerations.
tactical_explanations:
Repair bonus, circular design, durable products and urban mining belong in the vicinity of the circular economy. They keep value and material longer in the system.

The statement is true.

Sharing and durable designs are paths to a new kind of growth with lower environmental burden. They belong among the concrete approaches beside remanufacturing.

The statement is true.

Reconditioning used parts saves raw materials, lowers emissions and can create new economic opportunities. Remanufacturing connects resource conservation and value creation.

The statement is true.

Circular design aims at circularity and durability, not at single use. It stands in a line with durable products, not against them.

The statement is false.

The repair bonus is meant to extend use and postpone disposal. It belongs to circular considerations, not to linear take–make–waste logic.

The statement is false.

title: Poverty as a transformation task
context: Evaluate the following statements on poverty and sustainable transformation:
statements: With the transformation of the economy, widespread poverty should also be addressed as one of the most pressing problems.
Sub-Saharan Africa carries a disproportionate share of extreme poverty compared with its share of world population.
In Austria a different poverty definition applies than the worldwide extreme-poverty line: at risk of poverty is anyone below a threshold for a one-person household.
Poverty practically does not occur in Austria because poverty is mainly a topic outside Europe.
Progress in poverty reduction can stall through weak economic growth, pandemic aftermath and increasing fragility.
tactical_explanations:
The transformation of the economy should also address poverty. Sustainability without a social dimension would be incomplete.

The statement is true.

Although only about 16 percent of world population live there, about 67 percent of people in extreme poverty fall on sub-Saharan Africa. The share of poverty clearly lies above the population share.

The statement is true.

Worldwide the line of about 2.15 US dollars per day applies for extreme poverty; in Austria risk of poverty counts below a monthly threshold for a one-person household (about €1,572). The definitions differ.

The statement is true.

In Austria about 14.9 percent of the population were at risk of poverty — that corresponds to more than one million persons. Treating poverty as a purely extra-European topic misses national risk of poverty.

The statement is false.

Weak growth, COVID-19 aftermath and increasing fragility have stalled progress in poverty reduction. In low-income countries poverty rates sometimes lie higher than before the crisis.

The statement is true.

title: Growth against planetary boundaries
context: Evaluate the following statements on the dilemma of economic growth and ecological limits:
statements: Economic growth, understood as an increase in economic activities, is often seen as a central solution to reduce poverty.
The current level of global economic activities already exceeds several planetary boundaries.
A dilemma barely arises because growth lowers poverty and ecological limits are not touched in practice.
Measures to fight poverty can through their ecological impacts create new economic and social risks in the long run, especially when they rest on resource-intensive growth.
A sustainable transformation requires approaches that enable economic development within biophysical limits and promote social justice without crossing ecological tipping points.
tactical_explanations:
Growth is often seen as a central solution against poverty. Exactly this expectation creates the dilemma with planetary boundaries.

The statement is true.

The current level of global economic activities already exceeds several planetary boundaries and endangers the long-term ability to fulfil human needs.

The statement is true.

The dilemma consists precisely in this: growth is meant to lower poverty and finance public goods, but through resource and energy intensity threatens ecological stability. Denying both at once misses the challenge.

The statement is false.

Resource-intensive growth to fight poverty can create new risks in the long run. Ecological impacts feed back onto economy and society.

The statement is true.

Sustainable transformation needs development within biophysical limits with social justice, without crossing tipping points. That is the direction out of the dilemma.

The statement is true.

title: Our Common Future 1987
context: Evaluate the following statements on the Brundtland Report:
statements: The report Our Common Future was published in 1987 by the World Commission on Environment and Development (WCED).
It is also called the Brundtland Report because Gro Harlem Brundtland was the chair of the commission.
The report holds that the economic growth necessary to fight poverty must not, through its environmental impacts, lead to future economic problems.
Brundtland held the view that sustainable development is barely feasible because growth and environment can practically not be reconciled.
The report describes the extent of poverty and various threats to sustainability and calls for a new kind of economic growth with clearly lower environmental burden.
tactical_explanations:
Our Common Future appeared in 1987 with the WCED. The report shaped the discourse on poverty and sustainability.

The statement is true.

The name Brundtland Report refers to the chair Gro Harlem Brundtland. It is the same report, not a second document.

The statement is true.

Squaring the circle: necessary growth to fight poverty must not, through environmental effects, lead to future economic problems. Exactly that the report holds for possible and necessary.

The statement is true.

The report held sustainable development for necessary and feasible — a new kind of growth with lower environmental burden. Claiming impossibility reverses the position.

The statement is false.

Poverty and threats to sustainability are described; what is demanded is growth that burdens the environment far less and raises the ability of the joint system to satisfy people.

The statement is true.

title: Sustainable development according to Brundtland
context: Evaluate the following statements on the definition of sustainable development:
statements: Sustainable development is a form of economic growth that satisfies the needs and wishes of the present without endangering the ability of the economic and environmental system to fulfil these needs and wishes in the future.
What we need, according to the Brundtland Report, is a new kind of economic growth that burdens the environment far less.
Sustainability means mainly maximising today's profits; future needs play a secondary role.
This new kind of growth is meant to raise the ability of the joint system of economy and environment to satisfy people.
The Brundtland Report largely confines itself to technical questions of recycling and treats poverty only marginally.
tactical_explanations:
Fulfil present needs without endangering the future ability of the economic and environmental system: that is the Brundtland definition of sustainable development as a form of growth.

The statement is true.

A new kind of growth with far lower environmental burden — instead of endangering sustainability, the ability of the joint system to satisfy people is meant to rise.

The statement is true.

Sustainability aims at future need fulfilment, not at maximising today's profits. Otherwise the temporal dimension and the joint system would be empty.

The statement is false.

The new kind of growth is meant to raise the ability of the joint system of economy and environment to satisfy people. That connects poverty reduction and environmental protection.

The statement is true.

The report describes poverty and threats to sustainability at length. Recycling and sharing are paths, not the sole focus; poverty stands at the centre of the argument.

The statement is false.

title: European Green Deal and taxonomy
context: Evaluate the following statements on sustainability in European economic policy:
statements: Within the European Green Deal, sustainability has become a key term of European economic policy.
Sustainability reporting has been mandatory for large enterprises since 2022.
The EU taxonomy is meant to promote ecological business, for example through a better position on the capital market.
The European Green Deal mainly concerns forestry enterprises and barely counts as a key of EU economic policy.
The reporting duty named from 2022 applies without size difference equally to all enterprises.
tactical_explanations:
In the European Green Deal, sustainability is a key term of European economic policy. Reporting and taxonomy are concrete instruments.

The statement is true.

From 2022 sustainability reporting is mandatory for large enterprises — not for every micro-enterprise, but for the named large actors.

The statement is true.

The EU taxonomy is meant to promote ecological business, for example via a better position on the capital market. Capital allocation is coupled to ecological criteria.

The statement is true.

The Green Deal is a key of EU economic policy, not limited to forestry enterprises. Sustainability concerns economic policy as a whole.

The statement is false.

The reporting duty from 2022 applies to large enterprises, not without distinction to all. The size limit is part of the rule.

The statement is false.

title: Sustainability from forestry
context: Evaluate the following statements on the origin and expansion of the sustainability concept:
statements: Originally the term sustainability comes from forestry and denoted the practice of not felling more trees than can grow back.
This basic idea was meant to secure a lasting timber yield and preserve the tree stock.
The term sustainability is often used, yet its meaning often remains unclear.
Sustainability originally denoted mainly the maximisation of short-term enterprise profits.
The forestry basic idea has developed into a broader concept that comprises long-term ecological, social and economic developments.
tactical_explanations:
The origin lies in forestry: not felling more than grows back. Durability of the stock, not maximum harvest at any price.

The statement is true.

Lasting timber yield and preservation of the tree stock are the forestry purpose. Yield and stock protection belong together.

The statement is true.

Despite frequent use the meaning often remains unclear. Exactly therefore clarification of weak and strong sustainability and of the Brundtland definition is needed.

The statement is true.

Originally it was about sustainable timber yield, not short-term profit maximisation. The profit formula reverses the forestry basic idea.

The statement is false.

From the forestry core came a broader concept: long-term ecological, social and economic developments. The expansion still hangs on the idea of durability.

The statement is true.

title: Three pillars and weak sustainability
context: Evaluate the following statements on the concept of weak sustainability:
statements: Weak sustainability rests on the three-pillar model that treats ecology, the social sphere and the economy as equal pillars.
According to this concept, losses in one area can be offset by gains in another.
Natural resources can thereafter in principle be replaced by human knowledge or capital as long as the total sum of all capital types remains constant or grows.
Human capital means production plants in factories, while physical capital stands for education and qualification.
Natural capital comprises among other things forests, mineral resources and biodiversity.
tactical_explanations:
Weak sustainability rests on three equal pillars: ecology, the social sphere, the economy. Offset between the pillars is allowed.

The statement is true.

Losses in one area can be offset by gains in another. Substitutability between capital types is the core.

The statement is true.

As long as the sum of natural, human and physical capital holds or grows, natural resources may be replaced by knowledge or capital. That is the substitution logic of weak sustainability.

The statement is true.

The assignment is swapped: human capital stands for education and qualification, physical capital for production plants. Anyone who swaps the labels misses the capital types.

The statement is false.

Natural capital comprises forests, mineral resources and biodiversity — the ecological capital form beside human and physical capital.

The statement is true.

title: Stable climate as an irreplaceable function
context: Evaluate the following statements on the concept of strong sustainability:
statements: Strong sustainability assumes that certain ecological functions, for example a stable climate, are indispensable and cannot be replaced by any amount of economic or human capital.
This perspective rejects equating or substituting natural resources with other capital forms.
Strong sustainability demands preserving and protecting natural ecosystems as far as possible.
Strong sustainability counts as less demanding than the weak variant and therefore as dispensable.
Although it is clearly more demanding, strong sustainability is necessary to reach a sustainable economy within ecological limits.
tactical_explanations:
Certain ecological functions — for example a stable climate — are indispensable and not replaceable by economic or human capital. That is the core of strong sustainability.

The statement is true.

Equating and substitutability of natural resources with other capital forms are rejected. Natural capital remains irreplaceable in critical functions.

The statement is true.

Natural ecosystems are to be preserved and protected as far as possible. Preservation instead of offset through factories or education.

The statement is true.

Strong sustainability is clearly more demanding than the weak variant and necessary for a sustainable economy — not less demanding or dispensable.

The statement is false.

Despite higher demands, strong sustainability is needed to do business within ecological limits. Demand and necessity belong together.

The statement is true.

title: Forest loss against education funds
context: Evaluate the following statements on the difference between weak and strong sustainability:
statements: Offsetting forest loss through more human capital corresponds to the logic of weak sustainability, not strong.
A stable climate remains irreplaceable under strong sustainability even when physical capital and knowledge increase.
As long as an enterprise's stock-market value rises, planetary boundaries are largely complied with.
The three-pillar model of weak sustainability sets ecology, the social sphere and the economy as equal.
Strong sustainability allows critical ecosystem functions to be largely replaced as soon as factories become more productive.
tactical_explanations:
Offsetting forest loss through more education follows the substitution logic of weak sustainability. Strong sustainability would not replace critical ecological functions that way.

The statement is true.

A stable climate remains irreplaceable — more physical capital and knowledge change nothing about that under strong sustainability. Exactly this irreplaceability separates the concepts.

The statement is true.

Stock-market value says nothing about compliance with planetary boundaries. Financial valuation and biophysical load limits are different quantities.

The statement is false.

Three equal pillars — ecology, the social sphere, the economy — are the model of weak sustainability. Offset between the pillars is allowed.

The statement is true.

Strong sustainability precisely rejects replaceability of critical ecosystem functions. More productive factories do not replace a stable climate.

The statement is false.

title: Limits, cycle and reporting
context: Evaluate the following statements on linking the sustainability concepts of this section:
statements: Sharing models alone make any growth sustainable, regardless of biophysical limits.
The Brundtland Report holds the squaring for possible: necessary growth to fight poverty without future economic problems through environmental effects.
Linear take–make–waste and circular economy describe the same resource flow without essential difference.
Economic development within biophysical limits with simultaneous social justice is the direction of sustainable transformation.
External costs largely disappear as soon as a good has a market price, because that price contains the ecological and social follow-on damages.
tactical_explanations:
Sharing can lower environmental burden but does not make every growth sustainable. Biophysical limits remain the yardstick; a single model does not replace them.

The statement is false.

The squaring: growth to fight poverty must not, through environmental effects, lead to future economic problems. The report holds that for possible and necessary.

The statement is true.

Linear disposes after use; circular keeps resources in the system as long as possible. Those are opposite flows, not the same resource flow.

The statement is false.

Development within biophysical limits and social justice without tipping points — that is the transformation direction out of the growth–limits dilemma.

The statement is true.

Market prices often precisely do not contain external costs. Follow-on damages for society and ecosystem remain outside the price — that is the definition of external costs.

The statement is false.

title: Historical coupling of growth and environment
context: Evaluate the following statements on the coupling of economic growth and ecological burden:
statements: In the past, economic growth measured by GDP or income was closely linked to rising consumption of energy, raw materials and land as well as to growing emissions.
This coupling led to a steadily increasing ecological footprint that contributes substantially to exceeding several planetary boundaries.
Historically, energy consumption and emissions usually fell as soon as GDP rose.
A central aim of sustainable economic policy is to loosen the link between economic success and ecological burden.
The ecological footprint from this coupling contributes little to exceeding planetary boundaries.
tactical_explanations:
Historically, GDP growth and rising resource and emissions consumption ran in parallel. The coupling is the starting point for decoupling debates.

The statement is true.

From the coupling followed a growing ecological footprint that contributes substantially to exceeding several planetary boundaries.

The statement is true.

Historically consumption and emissions rose with GDP; they did not fall automatically. Absolute decoupling would be the opposite of this historical coupling.

The statement is false.

Sustainable economic policy wants to loosen the link between economic success and ecological burden — exactly that is what decoupling means.

The statement is true.

The footprint contributes substantially to exceeding planetary boundaries, not little. The coupling is ecologically consequential.

The statement is false.

title: Growth dilemma of politics
context: Evaluate the following statements on the political dilemma between growth and ecological stability:
statements: Many societal goals, for example employment, income security and social stability, are traditionally linked to economic growth.
Politics faces no real dilemma because growth usually strengthens ecological stability.
On the one hand growth is necessary to reduce poverty and finance public goods.
On the other hand the resource and energy intensity linked to growth threatens ecological stability.
Growth counts as largely superfluous for poverty reduction and financing public goods.
tactical_explanations:
Employment, income security and social stability are traditionally coupled to growth. Exactly therefore the political dilemma arises.

The statement is true.

The dilemma exists: growth is meant to secure social goals but through resource and energy intensity threatens ecological stability. Growth does not automatically strengthen ecology.

The statement is false.

Growth is seen as necessary to reduce poverty and finance public goods. That is one side of the dilemma.

The statement is true.

The other side: resource and energy intensity of growth threatens ecological stability. Both sides together yield the dilemma.

The statement is true.

Growth is precisely not treated as superfluous for poverty reduction and public goods — that would dissolve the dilemma by denying one side.

The statement is false.

title: Concept of decoupling
context: Evaluate the following statements on the concept of decoupling:
statements: Decoupling denotes the process in which economic development and environmental damages separate from each other.
The aim is to secure prosperity, employment and quality of life without resources consumption or emissions continuing to rise.
Decoupling means in essence largely shutting down economic activity.
Decoupling is desirable because it connects societal well-being with ecological carrying capacity.
The aim of decoupling is to continue economic activity outside Earth-system boundaries.
tactical_explanations:
Separating economic development and environmental damages from each other — that is decoupling. Not standstill, but dissolving the coupling.

The statement is true.

Prosperity, employment and quality of life are to be secured without further rising resource consumption or emissions. Absolute decoupling aims at falling burden while the economy grows.

The statement is true.

Decoupling does not shut down the economy but separates it from environmental damages. Standstill would be a different strategy.

The statement is false.

Decoupling connects societal well-being with ecological carrying capacity and enables economic activity within Earth-system boundaries.

The statement is true.

The aim is continuation within Earth-system boundaries, not outside. Outside would be continuation of the problematic coupling.

The statement is false.

title: Relative decoupling with a numerical example
context: Evaluate the following statements on relative decoupling:
statements: Relative decoupling is present when environmental damages increase more slowly than economic output.
A country whose GDP rises by 3% while CO₂ emissions rise by only 1% illustrates relative decoupling.
Under relative decoupling environmental burden already falls overall while GDP grows.
Emissions or resource consumption still rise under relative decoupling, but less strongly than GDP.
Relative decoupling is present when GDP rises by 3% and emissions fall by 4%.
tactical_explanations:
Environmental damages grow more slowly than economic output: relative decoupling. The burden continues to rise, only at a lower pace.

The statement is true.

GDP +3%, emissions +1%: classic example of relative decoupling. Both quantities rise; environmental burden more slowly.

The statement is true.

Under relative decoupling the burden does not yet fall absolutely; it only rises more slowly. Absolute decoupling would be the fall despite growing GDP.

The statement is false.

Still rising, but less strongly than GDP — exactly that marks relative decoupling versus absolute.

The statement is true.

GDP +3% and emissions −4% is absolute decoupling, not relative. The numbers swap the two forms.

The statement is false.

title: Absolute decoupling with a numerical example
context: Evaluate the following statements on absolute decoupling:
statements: Absolute decoupling means that environmental burden falls overall while economic output continues to increase.
If GDP rises by 3% and CO₂ emissions fall by 4%, absolute decoupling is present.
Absolute decoupling requires that GDP falls so that emissions can fall.
Only absolute decoupling ensures that economic development no longer occurs at the expense of ecological stability.
If GDP rises by 3% and emissions rise by 1%, that is already absolute decoupling.
tactical_explanations:
Burden falls, economy grows: absolute decoupling. That is more demanding than the relative form.

The statement is true.

GDP +3%, emissions −4% illustrates absolute decoupling. Environmental burden falls despite growing economic output.

The statement is true.

Absolute decoupling requires growing economic output with falling burden, not falling GDP. GDP decline would be shrinkage, not decoupling.

The statement is false.

Only absolute decoupling ensures that development no longer goes at the expense of ecological stability. Relative decoupling lets the burden continue to grow.

The statement is true.

GDP +3%, emissions +1% is relative decoupling. Absolute decoupling requires falling emissions.

The statement is false.

title: Absolute decoupling as a strategy
context: Evaluate the following statements on the importance of absolute decoupling in ecological economics:
statements: Absolute decoupling of economic output from environmental consumption counts in ecological economics as one of the central strategies for sustainable development.
It makes it possible to improve economic success and quality of life without exceeding planetary boundaries.
Relative decoupling already ensures that economic development does not occur at the expense of ecological stability.
Decoupling enables continuing economic activity within Earth-system boundaries.
Relative decoupling counts as a sufficient condition for ecological stability.
tactical_explanations:
Absolute decoupling is a central strategy of sustainable development in ecological economics. It separates success from environmental consumption.

The statement is true.

Improving economic success and quality of life without exceeding planetary boundaries — that is the promise of absolute decoupling.

The statement is true.

Relative decoupling lets the burden continue to rise, only more slowly. It precisely does not ensure that development does not go at the expense of ecology.

The statement is false.

Decoupling is meant to enable economic activity within Earth-system boundaries and connect well-being with carrying capacity.

The statement is true.

Only absolute decoupling is sufficient. Relative decoupling is progress but not a sufficient condition of ecological stability.

The statement is false.

title: Empirical evidence of decoupling
context: Evaluate the following statements on the empirical evidence of relative and absolute decoupling:
statements: So far relative decoupling has been achieved in many countries.
Absolute decoupling is demonstrable only in few areas and states.
Absolute decoupling has already been demonstrated for most pollutants in the majority of countries.
The empirical evidence is mixed: some countries have achieved absolute decoupling, most only relative, and some continue to strengthen the coupling between GDP and emissions.
Worldwide most regions have by now achieved absolute decoupling of economic growth and emissions.
tactical_explanations:
Relative decoupling has been achieved in many countries. Absolute decoupling remains rarer.

The statement is true.

Absolute decoupling only in few areas and states — that is the empirical finding, not blanket success.

The statement is true.

For most pollutants and the majority of countries absolute decoupling is precisely not demonstrated. The finding is selective, not blanket.

The statement is false.

Mixed evidence: some absolute decoupling, most relative, some strengthened coupling. The picture is differentiated.

The statement is true.

Most regions have not achieved absolute decoupling. Relative decoupling and partly strengthened coupling dominate.

The statement is false.

title: Local pollutants and CO₂
context: Evaluate the following statements on decoupling for SO₂, CFCs and CO₂:
statements: Absolute decoupling succeeded for some local pollutants, for example sulphur dioxide or CFCs, thanks to technical substitutes and international environmental agreements.
For CO₂ emissions absolute decoupling is clearly harder to achieve.
The same end-of-pipe logic that works for SO₂ already neutralises CO₂ at large scale.
Electrification of mobility, logistics and heat generation leads to efficiency gains and thus to falling energy demand.
Greenhouse gas emissions in industrial production are by now largely decoupled from energy consumption.
tactical_explanations:
SO₂ and CFCs: absolute decoupling succeeded via substitutes and agreements. Local pollutants are the success case.

The statement is true.

For CO₂ absolute decoupling is clearly harder. Industrial value creation remains tightly linked to energy consumption.

The statement is true.

For CO₂ a large-scale end-of-pipe technology that fully neutralises emissions is still lacking. Filter logic from SO₂ does not simply transfer.

The statement is false.

Electrification brings efficiency gains and falling energy demand in mobility, logistics and heat — a lever, but not a full CO₂ substitute.

The statement is true.

In industrial production greenhouse gas emissions remain tightly linked to energy consumption. Far-reaching decoupling there is precisely the problem.

The statement is false.

title: End-of-pipe and carbon capture
context: Evaluate the following statements on end-of-pipe technologies and CCS:
statements: For CO₂ no large-scale technology that fully neutralises emissions yet exists.
Processes such as carbon capture and storage are technically possible but expensive, energy-intensive and so far only usable to a limited extent.
For SO₂ or CFCs end-of-pipe technologies were developed, for example filters or substitution by less harmful substances.
CCS is comparatively inexpensive, energy-saving and already in nationwide use.
Carbon capture and storage already largely solves industrial CO₂ emissions.
tactical_explanations:
Large-scale full neutralisation of CO₂ is still lacking. That distinguishes CO₂ from pollutants with established end-of-pipe solutions.

The statement is true.

CCS is technically possible but expensive, energy-intensive and usable only to a limited extent. Possibility does not mean a nationwide solution.

The statement is true.

Filters and substitution worked for SO₂ and CFCs. End-of-pipe was the path there — for CO₂ the large-scale equivalent is missing.

The statement is true.

CCS is expensive and energy-intensive, not inexpensive and energy-saving; nationwide use is lacking. The properties are reversed.

The statement is false.

CCS does not largely solve industrial CO₂ emissions; deployment remains limited. The technology does not replace system transformation.

The statement is false.

title: CCS in Austria
context: Evaluate the following statements on the authorisation of CCS in Austria:
statements: In Austria CCS is allowed only for hard-to-abate industries.
Hard-to-abate industries are those for which it is currently expected that by 2040 no economically competitive carbon-free alternatives will yet exist.
Examples include parts of the waste and cement industries as well as aviation.
Austria allows CCS largely without industry-specific restriction.
For the named hard-to-abate areas, competitive carbon-free alternatives are already expected nationwide today.
tactical_explanations:
CCS in Austria is limited to hard-to-abate industries, not generally released.

The statement is true.

Hard-to-abate means: by 2040 no economically competitive carbon-free alternatives are expected. CCS here is an exception, not the normal case.

The statement is true.

Parts of the waste and cement industries as well as aviation are named examples. Exactly there the exception applies.

The statement is true.

Authorisation is industry-specifically limited, not largely without restriction. The limit to hard-to-abate is the point.

The statement is false.

Exactly for these areas no nationwide competitive alternatives are expected by 2040. Otherwise the CCS exception would not be needed.

The statement is false.

title: Carbon leakage
context: Evaluate the following statements on the relocation of emissions abroad:
statements: Even in countries with falling emissions, part of the reduction is attributable to relocating production and emissions to other world regions.
Carbon leakage means that emissions relocate abroad because production migrates to countries with laxer standards.
Falling national emissions usually prove that the global emissions of the same production have fallen to the same extent.
Absolute decoupling is not only a technological but above all a structural and institutional challenge.
If production migrates abroad, the inventory decline at home largely corresponds to the global climate effect.
tactical_explanations:
National emission declines can partly be carbon leakage: production and emissions migrate. Inventory falls; global load remains.

The statement is true.

Carbon leakage: emissions relocate because production migrates to countries with laxer standards. National balance and global effect diverge.

The statement is true.

National declines do not automatically prove global declines of the same production. Leakage can relativise the success.

The statement is false.

Absolute decoupling needs politics, system transformation and behavioural change — not only technology. Structurally and institutionally the challenge is larger.

The statement is true.

Inventory decline at home under leakage precisely does not correspond to the global climate effect. The emissions appear elsewhere.

The statement is false.

title: Rebound effects
context: Evaluate the following statements on rebound effects:
statements: Rebound effects can cancel efficiency gains again because more efficient technologies lower costs and often lead to higher overall demand for energy and goods.
Energy-efficient appliances can lead to more use.
Efficiency gains usually lower overall consumption automatically because cheaper energy use leads to less use.
A rebound effect is when efficiency gains lead to higher overall consumption.
If an appliance is more efficient, overall energy demand barely rises as a result.
tactical_explanations:
Efficiency lowers costs; higher demand can eat the saving. Rebound partly or fully cancels efficiency gains.

The statement is true.

Energy-efficient appliances can lead to more use — a classic rebound example. Less consumption per use does not mean less overall use.

The statement is true.

Cheaper energy use often leads to more, not less, use. Automatic lowering of overall consumption is therefore not given.

The statement is false.

Rebound: efficiency gains lead to higher overall consumption. Exactly this counter-movement makes absolute decoupling harder.

The statement is true.

More efficient appliances can precisely let overall energy demand rise if they are used more. “Barely” underestimates the rebound.

The statement is false.

title: Political and societal levers
context: Evaluate the following statements on what absolute decoupling requires:
statements: Absolute decoupling requires political measures, for example CO₂ pricing and support instruments for renewable energies.
It requires system transformations in energy, mobility and food systems.
It requires behavioural changes at consumer and enterprise level.
Technological innovations alone suffice for absolute decoupling at large scale.
Decisive are suitable political framework conditions, sustainable economic structures and societal values that promote ecological responsibility.
tactical_explanations:
CO₂ pricing and support for renewables are political levers of absolute decoupling. Technology alone does not suffice.

The statement is true.

Energy, mobility and food systems must be transformed. Absolute decoupling is a system question.

The statement is true.

Behaviour of consumers and enterprises belongs to it. Without behavioural change technical potentials remain unused.

The statement is true.

Technological innovations alone do not suffice. Politics, structures and values must move with them.

The statement is false.

Political framework conditions, sustainable structures and societal values are decisive. Absolute decoupling is carried institutionally and culturally as well.

The statement is true.

title: Partial absolute decoupling and net zero
context: Evaluate the following statements on partial absolute decoupling in affluent states:
statements: Some affluent states, for example the Scandinavian countries or the United Kingdom, have achieved partial absolute decoupling of GDP and CO₂ emissions.
Even there the reduction rates so far do not suffice to reach net-zero emissions by 2040 in industrial countries or by 2050 globally.
Decoupling is a precondition for long-term prosperity within ecological limits.
The reduction rates of those countries already suffice to secure climate neutrality by 2050.
Partial absolute decoupling means that the path to climate neutrality is already being kept.
tactical_explanations:
Scandinavia and the United Kingdom show partial absolute decoupling of GDP and CO₂. Success is local and partial, not globally nationwide.

The statement is true.

Even there the rates do not suffice for net zero by 2040 (industrial countries) or 2050 (global). Partial decoupling is not a target-achievement path.

The statement is true.

Decoupling is a precondition for long-term prosperity within ecological limits — not a technical side issue.

The statement is true.

The reduction rates so far do not suffice. Climate neutrality by 2050 is therefore not secured.

The statement is false.

Partial absolute decoupling means GDP and emissions have partly decoupled — not that the net-zero path is already being kept.

The statement is false.

title: Global trends 1990 to 2024
context: Evaluate the following statements on global trends of GDP, intensity and total emissions:
statements: Between 1990 and 2024 about 30 countries, mainly in the EU and in North America, absolutely reduced their CO₂ emissions while their GDP continued to grow.
In the same period CO₂ emissions per GDP unit fell globally by about 40%.
Nevertheless global total emissions continued to rise because economic growth overcompensated the efficiency gains.
Because emissions intensity fell globally by about 40%, global total emissions must have fallen by about 40% in the same period.
The reduction speed even in successful countries does not suffice to reach climate neutrality by 2050.
tactical_explanations:
About 30 countries have absolutely lowered emissions with continued GDP growth — mainly EU and North America. That is partial absolute decoupling, not the global trend.

The statement is true.

Emissions intensity (CO₂ per GDP) fell globally by about 40%. Intensity and total emissions are different quantities.

The statement is true.

Despite intensity gains, global total emissions rose because growth overcompensated the efficiency gains. Relative decoupling globally, not absolute.

The statement is true.

An intensity decline of 40% does not mean a total-emissions decline of 40%. Growth can overcompensate the intensity gain — exactly that happened globally.

The statement is false.

Even in successful countries the pace does not suffice for climate neutrality by 2050. Partial successes do not close the path.

The statement is true.

title: Required intensity rate and scale
context: Evaluate the following statements on the needed speed of decoupling and its reach:
statements: According to estimates global CO₂ intensity would have to fall by 8–9% annually; actually the rate is currently less than 2%.
Only if absolute decoupling succeeds at large scale can economic growth become compatible with climate neutrality and long-term prosperity.
An annual intensity decline of less than 2% already corresponds to the required path of 8–9%.
Decoupling is not a purely technical question but a fundamental precondition for reconciling prosperity and ecological stability.
According to mixed evidence most countries have already achieved absolute decoupling.
tactical_explanations:
Needed would be an 8–9% intensity decline per year; actually less than 2%. The gap between target and actual is large.

The statement is true.

Only absolute decoupling at large scale makes growth compatible with climate neutrality and long-term prosperity. Relative decoupling does not suffice for that.

The statement is true.

Less than 2% does not correspond to 8–9%. The actual rate clearly lies below the required path.

The statement is false.

Decoupling is a precondition for prosperity within ecological stability — politically, structurally and socially, not only technically.

The statement is true.

Mixed evidence: most countries have only relative decoupling; some strengthen the coupling. Absolute decoupling is the exception.

The statement is false.

title: Carbon budget as a guiding quantity
context: Evaluate the following statements on doing business within Earth-system boundaries and the carbon budget:
statements: Doing business with explicit regard to Earth-system boundaries means, for example, staying within the remaining carbon budget.
The carbon budget denotes the maximum amount of carbon dioxide that may still be emitted worldwide without exceeding a certain warming limit.
The carbon budget is usually stated in kilograms of methane, not in gigatonnes of CO₂.
Warming limits include among others the 1.5 °C or 2 °C above the pre-industrial level set in the Paris climate goals.
The budget barely rests on the link between cumulative greenhouse gas emissions and global warming.
tactical_explanations:
Earth-system boundaries in economic activity means concretely, for example: remaining in the remaining carbon budget. The budget is a guiding quantity for reduction targets.

The statement is true.
