Carbon budget = maximum still permissible CO₂ quantity without exceeding a warming limit. It is a cumulative quantity limit, not an annual target alone.

The statement is true.

The budget is stated in gigatonnes of CO₂ (GtCO₂), not in kilograms of methane. The unit follows the CO₂ link with warming.

The statement is false.

1.5 °C and 2 °C above the pre-industrial level are the named Paris limits to which the budget is oriented.

The statement is true.

The budget rests precisely on the scientific link between cumulative emissions and global warming. Without that link there would be no guiding quantity in GtCO₂.

The statement is false.

title: Remaining budget, pace and Austria
context: Evaluate the following statements on the remaining carbon budget and Austrian greenhouse gas emissions:
statements: The remaining carbon budget for 1.5 °C is 380 billion tonnes of CO₂, related to a probability of 50% of keeping warming below that.
At the current emissions rate this budget would be used up in only nine years.
In Austria greenhouse gas emissions began to fall for the first time in 2022.
The Austrian reduction already corresponds to the Effort Sharing Regulation.
The Effort Sharing Regulation does not require an adequate contribution to reducing global greenhouse gases.
tactical_explanations:
380 GtCO₂ at 50% probability for 1.5 °C: that is the named remaining budget. It is tightly measured.

The statement is true.

At today's emissions rate the budget would be used up in only nine years — not in decades. The pace of emissions determines the remaining lifetime.

The statement is true.

In 2022 Austrian GHG emissions began to fall for the first time. A first decline is not yet target fulfilment.

The statement is true.

The reduction does not correspond to the Effort Sharing Regulation. Falling alone does not suffice; the required contribution remains unmet.

The statement is false.

The Effort Sharing Regulation precisely requires an adequate contribution to reducing global greenhouse gases. Denying that misses the norm.

The statement is false.

title: 1.5 degrees as a political risk threshold
context: Evaluate the following statements on the 1.5-degree limit in relation to Earth-system boundaries:
statements: Johan Rockström and other climate researchers argue that the 1.5-degree limit is less a fixed Earth-system boundary than a political declaration of will.
Planetary boundaries result from complex interactions between biophysical and societal processes.
The 1.5-degree target setting rests primarily on political decision-making and scientific risk assessments.
The 1.5-degree limit constitutes an absolute biophysical boundary.
The climate crisis is the only Earth-system boundary defined by natural scientists.
tactical_explanations:
1.5 °C counts here rather as a political declaration of will than as a fixed Earth-system boundary. Planetary boundaries and climate target are related but not identical.

The statement is true.

Planetary boundaries arise from interactions of biophysical and societal processes — not from a single temperature target alone.

The statement is true.

Political decision and scientific risk assessment carry the 1.5-degree target setting. It is a chosen risk threshold.

The statement is true.

It is not an absolute biophysical boundary; it marks a politically chosen risk threshold. Even 1.5 °C has significant consequences but is not a hard Earth-system boundary in Rockström's sense.

The statement is false.

The climate crisis is one of several Earth-system boundaries. Nine boundaries were identified; climate is one of them.

The statement is false.

title: Paris 2015 and the IPCC special report
context: Evaluate the following statements on the international establishment of the 1.5-degree limit:
statements: The choice of the 1.5-degree limit as an international climate target goes back to the Paris Agreement of 2015.
The agreement was shaped substantially by pressure from particularly vulnerable states.
Scientific studies, in particular the IPCC special report of 2018, showed that even warming of 1.5 °C would have significant negative consequences for people and the environment.
The IPCC special report of 2018 showed that 1.5 °C remains largely without notable consequences for people and the environment.
Sea-level rise, species extinction and harvest declines barely count as possible consequences already at 1.5 °C.
tactical_explanations:
Paris 2015 made 1.5 °C the international climate target. The political anchoring sits there.

The statement is true.

Particularly vulnerable states exerted substantial pressure. The target choice is also an expression of their exposure.

The statement is true.

The IPCC special report 2018 showed significant negative consequences already at 1.5 °C — extreme weather, sea level, species extinction, harvests.

The statement is true.

“Without notable consequences” reverses the finding. Precisely the significant consequences justify the conservative threshold.

The statement is false.

Sea-level rise, species extinction and harvest declines are expressly named as possible consequences already at 1.5 °C.

The statement is false.

title: Tipping elements in the range 1.5 to 2 degrees
context: Evaluate the following statements on tipping elements of the Earth system:
statements: The named tipping elements include the Greenland and West Antarctic ice sheets, the Atlantic overturning circulation and tropical coral reefs.
These systems can undergo irreversible changes under continuing warming.
Numerous studies indicate that tipping elements can already enter critical phases in the range of 1.5 to 2 °C.
Uncertainty about the exact threshold values rather speaks against a conservative approach.
The named tipping elements become critical mainly only clearly above 3 °C and barely in the range of 1.5 to 2 °C.
tactical_explanations:
Ice sheets, Atlantic overturning circulation and tropical coral reefs are named tipping elements. They carry the special importance of the 1.5-degree threshold.

The statement is true.

Continuing warming can trigger irreversible changes. Tipping means: hard or impossible to reverse.

The statement is true.

Already in the range 1.5 to 2 °C critical phases can set in. Exactly therefore a conservative approach is taken.

The statement is true.

Uncertainty about threshold values speaks for, not against, a conservative approach. Caution is the answer to uncertainty.

The statement is false.

Many studies see critical phases already at 1.5–2 °C, not only clearly above 3 °C. The delay underestimates the risk.

The statement is false.

title: Nine identified Earth-system boundaries
context: Evaluate the following statements on the Earth-system boundaries identified by natural science:
statements: Nine Earth-system boundaries were identified, quantified and given limits whose exceedance leads to substantial risks and possible damages for people.
The named boundaries include climate, land-use change and integrity of the biosphere.
The introduction of novel substances and organisms counts among the identified Earth-system boundaries.
Above all climate and stratospheric ozone were defined as Earth-system boundaries; biochemical cycles and the availability of surface and groundwater barely belong to them.
Ocean acidification and aerosol loading of the atmosphere stand in the enumeration of the nine boundaries.
tactical_explanations:
Nine boundaries, quantified, with thresholds: exceedance carries substantial risks and damages for people. That is the framework of the concept.

The statement is true.

Climate, land-use change and integrity of the biosphere belong to the nine-item list. They are central processes of carrying capacity.

The statement is true.

Introduction of novel substances and organisms (novel entities) is one of the nine boundaries — beside climate, ocean acidification and others.

The statement is true.

Biochemical cycles and freshwater availability expressly belong. Narrowing to climate and ozone strikes out central boundaries.

The statement is false.

Ocean acidification and atmospheric aerosol loading are part of the nine. Aerosols still lie globally in the tolerance range but belong to the list.

The statement is true.

title: Damages, Earth system and coupling
context: Evaluate the following statements on consequences of exceeded boundaries and on linkage in the Earth system:
statements: Possible damages include lack of access to clean water and lower food security.
More unstable ecosystems or loss of jobs through rising temperatures or floods are named as consequences.
The Earth system comprises many interlinked processes such as the global carbon cycle, biological diversity or the chemical composition of the atmosphere.
If certain biophysical threshold values are exceeded, that can lead to irreversible changes that put the Earth system into a new, less stable state.
Because the systems are tightly connected, exceeding one boundary often remains isolated and barely affects other areas.
tactical_explanations:
Lack of access to clean water and lower food security are named damages of exceeded boundaries. The consequences hit people concretely.

The statement is true.

More unstable ecosystems and job losses through heat or floods belong among the consequences. Ecology and economy interlock.

The statement is true.

Carbon cycle, biological diversity and atmospheric chemistry are linked Earth-system processes. Stability and habitability hang on them.

The statement is true.

Exceeded thresholds can trigger irreversible changes and a less stable state. Tipping is the risk.

The statement is true.

Tightly connected means: exceeding one boundary often affects other areas. Isolation would be the opposite of coupling.

The statement is false.

title: Safe operating space according to Rockström
context: Evaluate the following statements on the planetary-boundaries concept and the safe operating space:
statements: The planetary-boundaries concept identifies nine central processes that determine the carrying capacity of the Earth system.
The aim is to define a safe operating space for humanity within which socio-economic activities can develop without endangering the stability of planetary systems.
To cope with the climate crisis, the other planetary boundaries must therefore also remain intact.
Socio-economic activities may strongly endanger the stability of planetary systems as long as one formally speaks of an operating space.
Currently the Earth is already clearly weakened in several of these dimensions.
tactical_explanations:
Nine central processes determine carrying capacity. The Rockström concept measures the safe space against that.

The statement is true.

Safe operating space: socio-economic activities without endangering planetary stability. Operating space is a limit, not a blank cheque.

The statement is true.

Solving the climate crisis alone does not suffice if other boundaries tear. The remaining boundaries must remain intact.

The statement is true.

Operating space means precisely not endangering stability at will. The concept limits activity; it does not justify it beyond the boundaries.

The statement is false.

Several dimensions are already clearly weakened. The current state lies in the global risk range.

The statement is true.

title: Seven exceeded boundaries 2025
context: Evaluate the following statements on the state of planetary boundaries according to Rockström et al. 2023 and the Planetary Health Check 2025:
statements: More than half of the nine planetary boundaries now count as exceeded.
For the climate system the indicators lie at about 1.2 °C of global warming and a CO₂ concentration above 420 ppm — both beyond the safe operating space.
Integrity of the biosphere counts as exceeded, among other things because species extinction rates reach more than a hundred times the natural level.
Exactly three of the nine planetary boundaries are exceeded; the remaining six lie clearly in the safe range.
Land-use change counts as exceeded among other things because agricultural use already makes up more than 70% of ice-free land area.
tactical_explanations:
Exceeded are seven of nine boundaries — hence clearly more than half. The wording requires the order of magnitude, not memorising the number seven.

The statement is true.

About 1.2 °C and CO₂ above 420 ppm mark the exceedance of the climate system. Both lie beyond the safe operating space.

The statement is true.

Species extinction rates above a hundred times the natural level justify the exceedance of biosphere integrity.

The statement is true.

Seven are exceeded, not three; only ozone and (globally aggregated) aerosols still count as within. The claim plays down the finding considerably.

The statement is false.

Land-use change is already exceeded at over about 40% agriculturally used ice-free area — not only at 70%. The 70% threshold is set too high.

The statement is false.

title: Ozone, aerosols and biochemical cycles
context: Evaluate the following statements on which boundaries are exceeded in 2025 and which lie in the safe range:
statements: Stratospheric ozone counts as within the safe range thanks to successful regeneration through international policy, namely the Montreal Protocol.
Atmospheric aerosol loading still lies globally aggregated within the tolerance range, but is already critical regionally.
Biochemical cycles of nitrogen and phosphorus count as exceeded, among other things because of widespread eutrophication and soil salinisation.
Freshwater availability remains unproblematic because withdrawals everywhere lie below regenerative capacity.
Ocean acidification with a pH drop of more than 0.1 since 1850 continues to count as within the safe operating space.
tactical_explanations:
The Montreal Protocol and regeneration keep stratospheric ozone in the safe range. International policy can protect boundaries.

The statement is true.

Globally aggregated still tolerant, regionally already critical: aerosols are the second boundary in the overall safe range with a regional warning signal.

The statement is true.

Nitrogen and phosphorus cycles are exceeded; eutrophication and soil salinisation are typical symptoms.

The statement is true.

Freshwater counts as exceeded: withdrawals lie above regenerative capacity. “Everywhere below capacity” is false.

The statement is false.

Ocean acidification with pH drop > 0.1 since 1850 counts as exceeded, not as within the safe operating space.

The statement is false.

title: Concentric circles and feedback
context: The state of planetary boundaries can be shown with a traffic-light system: green stands for the safe operating space, yellow for the risk zone and red for exceedance of critical thresholds. Evaluate the following statements on the current global risk status and on feedback effects:
statements: In the traffic-light system green marks the safe operating space, yellow the risk zone and red the exceedance of critical thresholds.
The current global finding shows that several systems are simultaneously in the yellow or red range because several critical thresholds are being exceeded at once.
An example of reinforcing feedback runs from climate change via biodiversity loss and lower CO₂ storage to further temperature rise.
In this system green stands for the strongest exceedance, while red marks the safe operating space.
Because the individual systems largely function independently, simultaneous exceedances barely strengthen feedback effects.
tactical_explanations:
Green = safe, yellow = risk, red = exceedance. The traffic light visualises the state of the boundaries.

The statement is true.

Several systems at once in the risk or exceedance range: global risk range. Simultaneity raises the danger of feedbacks.

The statement is true.

Climate change → biodiversity loss → lower CO₂ storage → further temperature rise: reinforcing feedback.

The statement is true.

Green and red are swapped. Green is the safe space, red the exceedance.

The statement is false.

The systems are tightly connected; simultaneous exceedances can strengthen feedbacks. Independence would be the wrong assumption.

The statement is false.

title: Climate risks and the Global South
context: Evaluate the following statements on unequally distributed climate risks and historical responsibility:
statements: Climate risks and responsibility are unequally distributed worldwide.
Risks include heavy precipitation, floods, droughts or avalanches.
Countries of the Global South have historically contributed little to CO₂ emissions but today feel the consequences of global warming particularly strongly.
Historical responsibility for emissions and today's exposure to climate impacts largely coincide worldwide on the same countries.
The Global South historically carries the largest share of cumulative emissions and remains largely spared from the consequences of global warming.
tactical_explanations:
Unequal distribution of risks and responsibility is the starting point of the climate-inequality debate.

The statement is true.

Heavy precipitation, floods, droughts, avalanches: typical climate risks. They hit with different strength.

The statement is true.

Little historical contribution, strong today's exposure: characteristic of the Global South. Responsibility and burden diverge.

The statement is true.

Responsibility and exposure precisely do not coincide. Those who have emitted little often feel more.

The statement is false.

Historically the Global South carries a small share (about 8%) but remains particularly exposed — not spared and not the main causer.

The statement is false.

title: Historical emissions shares
context: Evaluate the following statements on the historical shares of global emissions:
statements: Measured by historical emissions the USA are responsible for 40%.
The EU-28 historically stands for 29% of global emissions.
The Global South is historically responsible for 8% of global emissions.
The remaining Global North historically stands for 40% and the USA for 10%.
The rest of Europe historically stands for 13%, the remaining Global North for 10%.
tactical_explanations:
USA 40% of historical emissions: largest single block. Historical responsibility concentrates in the Global North.

The statement is true.

EU-28: 29%. Together with the USA the historical output dominates.

The statement is true.

Global South: 8%. The small share stands in contrast to strong today's exposure.

The statement is true.

Swapped: the USA stand for 40%, the remaining Global North for 10% — not the reverse. Swapping the numbers twists responsibility.

The statement is false.

Rest of Europe 13%, remaining Global North 10%: that closes the historical split. USA, EU-28 and rest of Europe carry the bulk.

The statement is true.

title: The richest percent and the top ten
context: Evaluate the following statements on inequality of carbon dioxide emissions between income groups:
statements: The richest percent of world population is responsible for twice as many carbon dioxide emissions as the poorest 50%.
The top 10% of emitters emitted on average 22 tonnes of CO₂ per capita in 2021.
22 tonnes of CO₂ per capita is more than 200 times as much as the average of the bottom 10%.
If the top 10% of emitters keep their current level, they alone will exceed the remaining carbon budget in the IEA net-zero scenario to 2050 by the year 2046.
The top 10% of emitters emit on average about 5 tonnes of CO₂ per capita and thus lie near the global mean.
tactical_explanations:
Richest 1% = twice as many emissions as the poorest 50%. Emissions inequality is extreme.

The statement is true.

22 tonnes of CO₂ per capita (2021) for the top 10%: far above what would be compatible with 1.5 °C.

The statement is true.

More than 200 times the bottom 10%: the spread is enormous. Per-capita comparisons make the inequality visible.

The statement is true.

The top 10% alone would, if they keep their level, blow the IEA net-zero budget by 2046. Fast decarbonisation of this group is needed.

The statement is true.

5 tonnes and nearness to the mean massively understates the top 10%; the average was 22 tonnes. The downplaying misses the inequality.

The statement is false.

title: Inequality within countries
context: Evaluate the following statements on emissions inequality within countries and on multiply burdened groups:
statements: Inequalities in emissions are by now larger within individual countries than between them.
A small, affluent population group causes through its consumption and investments a disproportionately high share of greenhouse gas emissions.
Socially disadvantaged groups are multiply burdened through low income, insecure employment or lack of education.
Disadvantaged groups are less affected by climate risks and can adapt more easily to changed conditions.
Climate protection measures such as a CO₂ tax can hit disadvantaged groups disproportionately because they must spend a larger share of their income on energy and basic provision.
tactical_explanations:
Within countries emissions inequality is by now larger than between countries. National averages conceal the spread.

The statement is true.

Small affluent groups cause disproportionately much through consumption and investments. Responsibility does not sit only between states.

The statement is true.

Multiple burden: low income, insecure work, lack of education. Climate risks hit these groups additionally.

The statement is true.

Disadvantaged people are more strongly affected and can adapt less well — not less and more easily. The direction is reversed.

The statement is false.

CO₂ taxes can act regressively because energy and basic provision bind a larger income share. Distributional effect belongs to climate policy.

The statement is true.

title: Poverty is not a sustainability ideal
context: Evaluate the following statements on the ecological footprint of poor groups and on the difference between scarcity and sustainability:
statements: Poorer population groups usually have a smaller ecological footprint.
Poverty counts as a sustainability ideal because low consumption automatically means sustainable living.
Low resource consumption often means restricted quality of life and limited social participation.
Low resource consumption must therefore not be confused with sustainable living.
Sustainable living and poverty can be equated because both describe the same forced resource scarcity.
tactical_explanations:
Poorer groups usually have a smaller footprint. That is empirically plausible but not a sustainability ideal.

The statement is true.

Poverty is not a sustainability ideal. Low consumption from scarcity is not the same as sustainable living within social and ecological limits.

The statement is false.

Low consumption often means restricted quality of life and limited participation. Scarcity is not sufficiency by choice.

The statement is true.

Therefore low resource consumption must not be confused with sustainable living. Sustainability demands a good life within the limits.

The statement is true.

Equating poverty and sustainability misses both: poverty is forced scarcity; sustainability aims at well-being within planetary boundaries.

The statement is false.

title: What the economy is for
context: Evaluate the following statements on the purpose and legitimacy of economic action:
statements: At the centre of economic considerations stands the question what the economy is for.
If the economy does not serve people's well-being, it loses its legitimacy.
Economic action aims mainly at maximising utility as a theoretical model quantity, not at promoting human welfare.
Economic action is judged by whether it serves human welfare — not only by whether model quantities such as utility are maximised.
Need, preference, utility, well-being, life satisfaction and happiness mean largely the same and can be swapped for one another.
tactical_explanations:
What the economy is for — that is the guiding question. Without clarifying purpose, economic technique remains without a yardstick.

The statement is true.

If the economy does not serve well-being, it loses its legitimacy. Purpose and justification hang on human welfare.

The statement is true.

The aim is to promote human welfare, not maximisation of the model quantity utility alone. Utility explains decisions but does not measure justice or sustainable well-being.

The statement is false.

The yardstick is human welfare; utility as a model quantity does not replace this purpose. The finer concepts (need, preference, utility, SWB) specify levels of this goal.

The statement is true.

The terms capture different levels — from objective preconditions to subjective perception. Arbitrary swapping blurs exactly this distinction.

The statement is false.

title: Needs as objective preconditions
context: Evaluate the following statements on needs as the basis of a life worthy of human dignity:
statements: Needs are objective preconditions of human existence.
Nutrition, health, belonging and security are examples of needs.
Needs are subjective evaluations and culturally shaped.
Needs mark what must be fulfilled so that people can lead a life worthy of human dignity.
Needs count as subjective preferences that can be socially shaped at will.
tactical_explanations:
Needs are objective: preconditions of existence, not mere wishes. That distinguishes them from preferences.

The statement is true.

Nutrition, health, belonging, security: typical needs. They mark minimum conditions of a life worthy of human dignity.

The statement is true.

Subjective and culturally shaped are preferences, not needs. Swapping the levels misses the ethical relevance of needs.

The statement is false.

What must be fulfilled for a life worthy of human dignity — that is the ethical relevance of needs. Minimum standard for justice.

The statement is true.

Preferences formable at will are preferences. Needs are objective preconditions, not socially arbitrarily formable wishes.

The statement is false.

title: Preferences and their distortions
context: Evaluate the following statements on preferences, culture and possible distortions:
statements: Preferences are subjective evaluations and culturally shaped.
Preferences can reflect needs but can also be distorted by advertising, status seeking or social comparisons.
Preferences are as a rule morally and ecologically desirable.
People can also have environmentally harmful or socially destructive preferences.
Preferences count, exactly like needs, as an objective minimum quantity for justice.
tactical_explanations:
Preferences are subjective and culturally shaped. They can mirror needs but need not.

The statement is true.

Advertising, status seeking and social comparisons can distort preferences. Therefore they are not a reliable mirror of objective needs.

The statement is true.

Preferences are not throughout morally or ecologically desirable. People can have environmentally harmful or socially destructive preferences.

The statement is false.

Environmentally harmful or socially destructive preferences are possible. Exactly therefore preference satisfaction does not suffice as a sustainability yardstick.

The statement is true.

The objective minimum quantity for justice is needs, not preferences. Preferences are socially formable and not throughout sustainable.

The statement is false.

title: Utility, SWB and life satisfaction
context: Evaluate the following statements on distinguishing utility, subjective well-being and life satisfaction:
statements: Utility denotes the short-term satisfaction that arises from satisfying a preference.
Subjective well-being and life satisfaction refer to the overall judgement of one's own life, not only to momentary pleasure.
Utility at the same time measures justice and sustainability.
Economic growth can raise utility and nevertheless diminish well-being if social inequality, stress or environmental destruction increase.
Subjective well-being can be equated with short-term, momentary pleasure.
tactical_explanations:
Utility = short-term satisfaction from preference satisfaction. It is an analytical model quantity, not an overall judgement of life.

The statement is true.

SWB and life satisfaction aim at the sustainable quality of existence, the overall judgement — not only momentary pleasure.

The statement is true.

Utility is value-neutral: it measures what individuals want, not justice or sustainability. Exactly that separates it from well-being.

The statement is false.

Growth can raise utility and nevertheless diminish well-being if inequality, stress or environmental destruction increase. Utility and SWB do not automatically run in parallel.

The statement is true.

Short-term pleasure is rather happiness as an affective component; SWB and life satisfaction mean the overall judgement. Equating blurs the levels.

The statement is false.

title: Six concepts in overview
context: Evaluate the following statements on distinguishing the concepts around well-being:
statements: Needs describe basic preconditions for a good life and lie on the objective level.
Utility is a theoretical model quantity for explaining decisions and describes decision behaviour, not well-being.
Happiness stands for the long-term assessment of one's own life.
Life satisfaction is a long-term assessment of one's own life and counts empirically as a measure of the success of politics and institutions.
Subjective well-being is like utility a purely analytical model quantity that only describes decision behaviour.
tactical_explanations:
Needs = objective preconditions of a good life, minimum standard for justice. That is the lowest ethical level.

The statement is true.

Utility explains decisions but does not measure well-being. Analytical model quantity ≠ empirical overall judgement.

The statement is true.

Happiness means short-term positive emotions (affective). The long-term assessment is life satisfaction.

The statement is false.

Life satisfaction = long-term assessment; empirical measure of political and institutional success. That matches the table.

The statement is true.

SWB is an empirical evaluation of life (emotional and cognitive), not a purely analytical model quantity like utility.

The statement is false.

title: Why the distinction is needed
context: Evaluate the following statements on why need, preference, utility and well-being must be kept separate:
statements: Distinguishing the terms helps to better align economic, social and ecological goals.
Only if the concepts are distinguished can economics at the same time explain how people decide, what they need and how well they actually are.
Utility is value-neutral: it measures what individuals want, not justice or sustainability.
Well-being and life satisfaction barely give indications of whether societal systems contribute to a good life.
Preferences are as a rule a reliable mirror of objective needs.
tactical_explanations:
Separate terms enable aligning economic, social and ecological goals. Mixing creates false policy yardsticks.

The statement is true.

Deciding (utility/preference), needing (needs) and actual faring (SWB) explained at once — only with clear distinction.

The statement is true.

Utility measures wanting, not justice or sustainability. Value neutrality is strength and limit of the concept.

The statement is true.

Well-being and life satisfaction precisely give indications whether systems contribute to a good life. That is their empirical role.

The statement is false.

Preferences can be distorted and only partly mirror needs. They are not a reliable mirror.

The statement is false.

title: Income and life satisfaction
context: Evaluate the following statements on the empirical link between income and life satisfaction:
statements: Empirical findings show that income correlates with life satisfaction only up to a certain threshold.
Health, social relationships, trust and participation are more important than an unlimited income link.
Above every income level life satisfaction continues to rise proportionally and without a threshold.
The World Happiness Report 2025 is named alongside work by Ferrer-i-Carbonell as a line of evidence.
Income is the only empirical determinant of life satisfaction.
tactical_explanations:
Only up to a threshold does income correlate with life satisfaction. Above that other factors gain weight.

The statement is true.

Health, relationships, trust, participation weigh more heavily than unlimited income growth. Empirics relativise GDP as a happiness measure.

The statement is true.

Without a threshold and proportionally unlimited further: that contradicts the threshold finding. Diminishing increments and other determinants apply.

The statement is false.

Ferrer-i-Carbonell and the World Happiness Report 2025 support the empirical line. Several sources, not only income tables.

The statement is true.

Income is not the only factor. Health, relationships, trust, unemployment and education count as well.

The statement is false.

title: Comparisons, unemployment and education
context: Evaluate the following statements on relative comparisons, uncertainty and education as determinants of well-being:
statements: People evaluate their happiness relative to others.
Unemployment and uncertainty diminish well-being more strongly than income losses.
Education raises life satisfaction via self-efficacy and employment prospects.
Relative comparisons play a secondary role for the happiness judgement.
Income losses as a rule diminish well-being more strongly than unemployment.
tactical_explanations:
Relative comparisons shape the happiness judgement. Absolute income alone explains less than the position relative to others.

The statement is true.

Unemployment and uncertainty hit harder than pure income losses. Status and security weigh heavily.

The statement is true.

Education acts on life satisfaction via self-efficacy and employment prospects — not only via higher income.

The statement is true.

Relative comparisons are central, not secondary. People evaluate happiness relative to others.

The statement is false.

Unemployment and uncertainty diminish more strongly than income losses — not the reverse. Swapping the ranking misses the finding.

The statement is false.

title: Happy countries and young people
context: Evaluate the following statements on the World Happiness Report and life satisfaction of young people:
statements: The World Happiness Report 2025 shows that countries with high values for social trust, institutional quality and environmental awareness are at the same time the happiest.
Scandinavia, the Netherlands and New Zealand count as examples of such countries.
For young people life satisfaction depends strongly on meaning, security and social inclusion.
The report attributes the happiness of these countries mainly to particularly high per-capita income.
For young people life satisfaction hangs mainly on material consumption, less on meaning or social inclusion.
tactical_explanations:
Trust, institutional quality and environmental awareness mark the happiest countries. Income alone does not explain the ranking.

The statement is true.

Scandinavia, the Netherlands, New Zealand: examples of high values on these dimensions and at the same time high happiness scores.

The statement is true.

Meaning, security, social inclusion: central determinants of young people's life satisfaction. Matter alone does not suffice.

The statement is true.

The report stresses trust, institutions and environmental awareness, not per-capita income alone. Reducing the explanation to income would be too narrow.

The statement is false.

Young people increasingly link happiness to meaning and inclusion, not mainly to material consumption. The weighting is reversed.

The statement is false.

title: Youth, climate anxiety and meaning
context: Evaluate the following statements on young people's concerns and on linking happiness with sustainability:
statements: In Europe according to Gallup data 2023 almost 60% of 18- to 29-year-olds express concerns about the future of climate and society.
Young people increasingly link happiness with meaningfulness, nature experience and co-shaping rather than with material consumption.
These empirical trends show that well-being in the 21st century is inseparably linked with sustainability.
Young people increasingly link happiness mainly with material consumption.
The named Gallup data 2023 describe all age groups worldwide with the same percentage figure of almost 60%.
tactical_explanations:
Almost 60% of 18- to 29-year-olds in Europe express climate and society concerns. Future anxiety is age- and region-related.

The statement is true.

Meaning, nature experience, co-shaping rather than material consumption: shift in the definition of happiness among young people.

The statement is true.

Well-being and sustainability are linked in the 21st century. The empirical trends support this coupling.

The statement is true.

The shift goes away from material consumption towards meaning and co-shaping — not back towards it.

The statement is false.

The figure applies to 18- to 29-year-olds in Europe, not to all age groups worldwide. The generalisation is false.

The statement is false.

title: Doughnut: social foundation and ecological ceiling
context: Evaluate the following statements on Kate Raworth's Doughnut model:
statements: Kate Raworth's Doughnut connects a social foundation (basic needs for all) with an ecological ceiling (planetary load limits).
The area between these rings is the safe and just operating space.
The model mainly connects ecological target quantities and knows no social foundation.
The aim of a sustainable economy is a good life for all within planetary boundaries.
The ecological ceiling in the model denotes the social foundation of poorer countries.
tactical_explanations:
Social foundation inside, ecological ceiling outside: two target quantities. The Doughnut connects justice and planetary boundaries.

The statement is true.

Between the rings lies the safe and just operating space. Below it scarcity, above it ecological exceedance.

The statement is true.

The model expressly knows a social foundation. Seeing only ecology strikes out half the construction.

The statement is false.

A good life for all within planetary boundaries: aim of a sustainable economy in the Doughnut sense.

The statement is true.

Ecological ceiling = planetary load limits, not the social foundation. Swapping foundation and ceiling twists the model.

The statement is false.

title: Doughnut Monitor 2025
context: Evaluate the following statements on the empirical finding of the Doughnut Monitor 2025:
statements: No country at once fulfils all social minimum standards and stays within the ecological limits.
Rich countries typically exceed the ecological limits.
Poorer countries typically undershoot the social foundation.
Several countries already fulfil all social minimum standards without exceeding ecological limits.
Rich countries typically undershoot the social foundation, while poorer countries tear the ecological ceiling.
tactical_explanations:
No country achieves both at once: all social minimum standards and compliance with ecological limits. The Doughnut Monitor 2025 shows the gap.

The statement is true.

Rich countries tear the ecological ceiling. Prosperity often goes with overuse.

The statement is true.

Poorer countries undershoot the social foundation. Lack of basic needs, not necessarily ecological overuse.

The statement is true.

Precisely no country fulfils all social standards within the limits. “Several countries” contradicts the finding.

The statement is false.

The assignment is swapped: the rich exceed ecology, the poor undershoot the social — not the reverse.

The statement is false.

title: Consumption corridor between minimum and maximum
context: Evaluate the following statements on the consumption corridor:
statements: A consumption corridor sets the range between a social minimum and an ecological maximum.
Undernutrition lies below the social minimum.
Excessive meat and energy consumption lie above the ecological maximum.
The consumption corridor knows mainly an upper limit and barely a social minimum.
Undernutrition in the example lies above the ecological maximum.
tactical_explanations:
Social minimum below, ecological maximum above: between them the consumption corridor. Enough, but not too much.

The statement is true.

Undernutrition lies below the minimum — scarcity, not sustainability. The corridor begins only above this scarcity.

The statement is true.

Excessive meat and energy consumption lie above the maximum. Overconsumption bursts the ecological ceiling.

The statement is true.

The corridor has a lower and an upper limit. Only an upper limit without a social minimum would be incomplete.

The statement is false.

Undernutrition lies below the social minimum, not above the ecological maximum. The assignment is swapped.

The statement is false.

title: Production corridor and needs
context: Evaluate the following statements on the production corridor:
statements: A production corridor describes which goods and services should be produced in which form in order to satisfy needs without exceeding ecological limits.
These concepts tie directly to subjective well-being.
The production corridor mainly sets market prices and says little about types of goods or forms of production.
The aim of the described production is the satisfaction of needs within ecological limits.
The production corridor replaces needs with pure utility as the yardstick of what should be manufactured.
tactical_explanations:
Which goods and services, in which form, for needs without exceeding limits: that is the production corridor.

The statement is true.

Consumption and production corridors tie to subjective well-being. Sufficiency and diminishing increments connect production and SWB.

The statement is true.

It is about types of goods and forms of production, not about setting market prices. Price formation is another topic.

The statement is false.

Need satisfaction within ecological limits is the production aim in the corridor. Need and limit belong together.

The statement is true.

The yardstick is needs within ecological limits, not pure utility. Utility does not replace needs here.

The statement is false.

title: Sufficiency and diminishing increments
context: Evaluate the following statements on excessive consumption, sufficiency and well-being:
statements: Studies show that excessive consumption brings diminishing increments of satisfaction.
Sufficiency, understood as enough but not too much, generates more stable well-being in the long run.
Sufficiency means consuming as much as possible as long as utility rises.
Consumption and production corridors are expressly bound to subjective well-being.
Unlimited consumption raises well-being largely linearly and without diminishing increments.
tactical_explanations:
Excessive consumption brings diminishing increments of satisfaction. More consumption does not mean proportionally more well-being.

The statement is true.

Enough, but not too much: sufficiency stabilises well-being better in the long run than overconsumption.

The statement is true.

Sufficiency limits; it does not maximise consumption as long as utility rises. The definition reverses the term.

The statement is false.

The corridors tie directly to SWB. Production and consumption are measured by well-being, not only by output.

The statement is true.

Diminishing increments and sufficiency contradict well-being rising linearly without limit through consumption.

The statement is false.

title: Growth, utility and diminished well-being
context: Evaluate the following statements on the tension between growth, utility and sustainable well-being:
statements: Economic growth can raise utility and nevertheless diminish well-being if social inequality, stress or environmental destruction are intensified.
This distinction between utility and well-being is decisive.
If growth raises utility, well-being as a rule rises to the same extent with it.
If the economy does not serve people's well-being, it loses its legitimacy.
Subjective well-being is largely identical with the short-term satisfaction from fulfilling a single preference.
tactical_explanations:
Utility high, well-being low: possible with inequality, stress, environmental destruction. Growth is not an automatic SWB gain.

The statement is true.

Without distinguishing utility and well-being every utility plus would count as success — even with falling quality of life.

The statement is true.

Equal rise of utility and well-being is not given. Exactly the decoupling of both quantities is the decisive point.

The statement is false.

Legitimacy hangs on people's well-being. An economy without this purpose loses its justification.

The statement is true.

Short-term preference satisfaction is utility; SWB is the overall judgement of life. Equating blurs the levels.

The statement is false.

title: Environmental quality and life satisfaction
context: Evaluate the following statements on the link between environmental quality and life satisfaction:
statements: Clean air, green spaces and intact ecosystems measurably raise life satisfaction.
Noise, air pollution and land sealing lower life satisfaction.
Noise measurably raises life satisfaction.
The named environmental factors empirically affect life satisfaction.
Land sealing measurably raises life satisfaction.
tactical_explanations:
Clean air, green spaces and intact ecosystems raise life satisfaction measurably. Environmental quality is a happiness factor.

The statement is true.

Noise, air pollution and land sealing lower it. Environmental burdens weigh on subjective well-being.

The statement is true.

Noise lowers life satisfaction; it does not raise it. The direction of the effect is reversed.

The statement is false.

Positive and negative environmental factors empirically affect life satisfaction. The environment is not a side stage of well-being.

The statement is true.

Land sealing lowers life satisfaction; it does not raise it. Sealing belongs among the burdening factors.

The statement is false.

title: Nature connectedness and mental health
context: Evaluate the following statements on nature connectedness, mental health and resilience:
statements: Nature connectedness strengthens mental health and resilience.
Nature connectedness weakens mental health.
Empirical studies link environmental quality with measurable life satisfaction.
Above all income determines life satisfaction; environmental quality plays a secondary role.
Intact ecosystems belong among the factors that raise life satisfaction.
tactical_explanations:
Nature connectedness strengthens mental health and resilience. Closeness to nature is a well-being factor.

The statement is true.

Strengthen, not weaken: nature connectedness acts positively on mental health. Reversing the direction contradicts the finding.

The statement is false.

Environmental quality and life satisfaction hang together empirically. Clean air and green spaces raise; noise and sealing lower.

The statement is true.

Environmental quality plays a clear role beside income. Dismissing it as secondary underestimates the empirical finding.

The statement is false.

Intact ecosystems raise life satisfaction. They stand on the plus side of the same environmental logic as clean air and green spaces.

The statement is true.

title: Healthy Lifetime Income according to Prettner
context: Evaluate the following statements on the Healthy Lifetime Income indicator:
statements: With the Healthy Lifetime Income indicator, countries with higher life expectancy and better health care reach clearly higher well-being, even with more moderate material prosperity.
The indicator ties well-being to life expectancy and health care, not to material prosperity alone.
More moderate material prosperity rules out any higher well-being.
Health and life expectancy count in this finding beside material prosperity.
The indicator shows that above all the highest income generates higher well-being.
tactical_explanations:
Higher life expectancy and better care → higher well-being, even with more moderate material prosperity. Health counts.

The statement is true.

Not material prosperity alone: life expectancy and health care carry the level as well. The indicator widens the view beyond income.

The statement is true.

Precisely with more moderate material prosperity well-being can lie higher if health and life expectancy are strong. Exclusion would be false.

The statement is false.

Health and life expectancy count beside material prosperity. Several dimensions, not only purchasing power.

The statement is true.

Highest income alone is not the finding; health and life expectancy contribute at more moderate prosperity. An income monopoly contradicts the indicator.

The statement is false.

title: Happiness beyond pure income growth
context: Evaluate the following statements on which economic orientation raises happiness more strongly in the long run:
statements: An economy that strengthens health, environmental quality and social stability raises happiness more strongly in the long run than pure income growth.
Pure income growth raises happiness more strongly in the long run than an economy that strengthens health, environmental quality and social stability.
This conclusion follows from the finding on Healthy Lifetime Income.
Social stability plays a secondary role for this link and can be neglected.
Long-term happiness in this argument does not hang on income growth alone.
tactical_explanations:
Health, environmental quality and social stability beat pure income growth in the long run. Happiness follows the quality of living conditions.

The statement is true.

The ranking is reversed: pure income growth is the weaker long-term motor. Health, environment and stability weigh more heavily.

The statement is false.

From Healthy Lifetime Income it follows: health and life expectancy carry well-being even at more moderate material prosperity — and thus priority beyond pure income growth.

The statement is true.

Social stability belongs to the triad health–environment–stability. Dismissing it as negligible strikes out one of the three levers.

The statement is false.

Not income growth alone: long-term happiness also hangs on health, environmental quality and social stability.

The statement is true.

title: Well-being in a social context
context: Evaluate the following statements on trust, cooperation and equality as factors of well-being:
statements: Well-being arises in a social context.
Trust, cooperation and equality are central factors.
Well-being arises largely independently of social relationships, mainly through individual income.
Equality belongs among the central factors, not only trust.
Cooperation counts as secondary relative to GDP.
tactical_explanations:
Well-being arises in a social context, not isolated in the individual. Relationships and institutions contribute.

The statement is true.

Trust, cooperation and equality are central factors. The social fabric shapes happiness scores.

The statement is true.

Independence from social relationships and income alone contradict the social context. GDP alone does not explain happiness differences.

The statement is false.

Equality stands beside trust and cooperation in the central factors list. Not trust only.

The statement is true.

Cooperation is central, not secondary to GDP. Similar GDP with different cooperation and equality leads to different happiness scores.

The statement is false.

title: Equality and World Happiness Report
context: Evaluate the following statements on social equality and the happiness scores of the World Happiness Report:
statements: Societies with high social equality (for example Scandinavia) show according to the World Happiness Report the highest happiness scores.
The World Happiness Report places Scandinavian societies despite high equality rather at the lower end of happiness scores.
High social equality is linked with the highest happiness scores.
Above all GDP explains the ranking of happiness scores.
Scandinavia serves as an example of societies with high social equality.
tactical_explanations:
High equality and highest happiness scores coincide in Scandinavia. The report supports this link.

The statement is true.

Scandinavia lies at the upper, not the lower, end. High equality and high happiness scores belong together.

The statement is false.

High social equality is linked with the highest happiness scores. Equality is a happiness factor, not only morals.

The statement is true.

GDP alone does not explain the ranking; with similar GDP unequal or corrupt countries lie lower. Institutions and equality count.

The statement is false.

Scandinavia is the example of high social equality with high happiness scores. The geographic reference is correct.

The statement is true.

title: Inequality, corruption and similar GDP
context: Evaluate the following statements on happiness scores under inequality or corruption despite similar GDP:
statements: Countries with strong inequality or corruption (for example Brazil, South Africa) lie clearly lower, even with similar GDP.
With similar GDP countries as a rule lie on the same happiness level.
Brazil and South Africa are named examples of lower happiness scores under inequality or corruption.
Corruption remains without notable influence on happiness scores once GDP is comparable.
Inequality or corruption can lower the happiness level despite similar GDP.
tactical_explanations:
With similar GDP Brazil and South Africa lie clearly lower when inequality or corruption are strong. GDP does not level happiness scores.

The statement is true.

Similar GDP does not mean the same happiness level. Inequality and corruption lower the scores despite comparable economic output.

The statement is false.

Brazil and South Africa are the named examples. They illustrate the gap despite similar GDP.

The statement is true.

Corruption influences happiness scores even with comparable GDP. “Without influence” contradicts the finding.

The statement is false.

Inequality or corruption can depress happiness despite similar GDP. Social and institutional factors count beside GDP.

The statement is true.

title: Participatory education and young people
context: Evaluate the following statements on life satisfaction and future anxiety of young people in participatory education systems:
statements: Young people in countries with participatory education systems report higher life satisfaction.
The same young people report lower future anxiety.
Participatory education systems raise young people's future anxiety.
Above all adults, not young people, are the subject of this education finding.
Participation in the education system is linked with higher life satisfaction and lower future anxiety.
tactical_explanations:
Participatory education hangs together with higher life satisfaction of young people. Co-shaping strengthens subjective well-being.

The statement is true.

At the same time lower future anxiety: participation dampens anxiety and raises satisfaction. Both belong to the finding.

The statement is true.

Participation lowers future anxiety; it does not raise it. Reversing the direction contradicts the finding.

The statement is false.

The subject is young people in participatory education systems, not mainly adults. Swapping the target group misses the point.

The statement is false.

Higher life satisfaction and lower future anxiety: the dual effect of participation in the education system.

The statement is true.

title: Stability and sustainability as means
context: Evaluate the following statements on the role of economic stability and ecological sustainability:
statements: Economic stability and ecological sustainability are means, not ends in themselves.
They serve to give people the freedom to lead a good life.
Ecological sustainability is an end in itself and independent of the good life.
Freedom to a good life is the goal that stability and sustainability serve.
Economic stability counts as an end goal to which the good life is subordinated.
tactical_explanations:
Stability and sustainability are means, not ends in themselves. The purpose is the good life.

The statement is true.

Means to the freedom to lead a good life: that is the ends–means logic. Economy and ecology serve people.

The statement is true.

As an end in itself independent of the good life, sustainability would be framed wrongly. It remains a means to freedom for a good life.

The statement is false.

Freedom to a good life is the goal; stability and sustainability serve it. End and means are clearly ordered.

The statement is true.

Economic stability is a means, not an end goal. Subordinating the good life to GDP reverses the logic.

The statement is false.

title: Three dimensions of a sustainable economy
context: Evaluate the following statements on the three dimensions a sustainable economy must integrate:
statements: A sustainable economy must integrate three dimensions.
The social dimension requires satisfying everyone's needs and reducing inequalities.
Two dimensions, only social and ecological, suffice.
The ecological dimension requires staying within planetary boundaries.
The psychological dimension is left out of the threefold list.
tactical_explanations:
Three dimensions: social, ecological, psychological. Integration, not selection of one.

The statement is true.

Social: everyone's needs, less inequality. That is the justice side of a sustainable economy.

The statement is true.

Two dimensions do not suffice; the psychological (SWB and meaning) belongs. Without it subjective well-being as a target quantity is missing.

The statement is false.

Ecological: stay within planetary boundaries. Without this dimension the biophysical limit is missing.

The statement is true.

The psychological dimension stands expressly in the threefold list. Leaving it out would be a shortening.

The statement is false.

title: Psychological dimension of sustainability
context: Evaluate the following statements on the psychological dimension of a sustainable economy:
statements: The psychological dimension is meant to enable subjective well-being and meaning.
Meaning plays a secondary role in the three dimensions.
Subjective well-being belongs to the psychological dimension, not only material utility.
The psychological dimension largely replaces the social and the ecological.
All three dimensions must be integrated; they are not optionally choosable one after another.
tactical_explanations:
SWB and meaning: content of the psychological dimension. A sustainable economy without meaning and well-being would be incomplete.

The statement is true.

Meaning belongs centrally to the psychological dimension, not secondarily. Leaving it out strikes out half of this dimension.

The statement is false.

Subjective well-being, not only material utility: the psychological dimension goes beyond utility maximisation.

The statement is true.

It must not replace the social and ecological dimensions. All three must be integrated.

The statement is false.

Integration is mandatory; there is no optional sequence. A sustainable economy needs all three at once.

The statement is true.

title: Where well-being arises
context: Evaluate the following statements on the conditions under which well-being arises:
statements: Well-being arises where needs are fulfilled, ecological stability is preserved and social relationships are cultivated.
Ecological stability is dispensable for the arising of well-being if needs are fulfilled.
Social relationships belong to the arising of well-being.
Fulfilled needs largely suffice; relationships and ecological stability then drop away.
The three conditions stand side by side, not as substitutes for one another.
tactical_explanations:
Needs, ecological stability and social relationships: there well-being arises. Three conditions, one place.

The statement is true.

Ecological stability is not dispensable. Without it one of the three conditions is missing.

The statement is false.

Social relationships belong to arising. Well-being is socially embedded.

The statement is true.

Needs alone do not suffice; relationships and ecological stability remain necessary. Shortening to one condition misses the closing sentence.

The statement is false.

Side by side, not substitutes: the three conditions complement each other. One cannot replace the others.

The statement is true.

title: Environmental burdens and social inequality together
context: Evaluate the following statements on the interplay of environmental quality, equality and happiness scores:
statements: Noise, air pollution and land sealing lower life satisfaction, while clean air, green spaces and intact ecosystems raise it.
High social equality and high happiness scores coincide in the World Happiness Report in Scandinavian societies.
With similar GDP, environmental quality and equality barely still need to differentiate happiness scores because domestic product already explains a lot.
Nature connectedness strengthens mental health and resilience and thus stands on the plus side of the same environmental logic as clean air and green spaces.
Brazil and South Africa lie clearly lower despite possible similar GDP because strong inequality or corruption burden happiness scores.
tactical_explanations:
Environmental burdens lower, environmental quality raises life satisfaction. Both directions belong to the empirical environment–well-being logic.

The statement is true.

Scandinavia: high equality and high happiness scores. The report links both.

The statement is true.

With similar GDP, environmental quality, equality and corruption continue to differentiate happiness scores. GDP does not explain everything.

The statement is false.

Nature connectedness belongs on the plus side like clean air and green spaces. Mental health and resilience benefit.

The statement is true.

Inequality or corruption depress happiness despite similar GDP; Brazil and South Africa illustrate that. Institutions and distribution count.

The statement is true.

title: Health, income and happiness comparisons
context: Evaluate the following statements on the relation of Healthy Lifetime Income, material prosperity and happiness comparisons:
statements: Countries can reach clearly higher well-being when life expectancy and health care are better, even with only more moderate material prosperity.
Pure income growth remains the stronger long-term motor of happiness compared with health, environmental quality and social stability.
Similar GDP does not automatically set Brazil or South Africa on the same happiness level as societies with high social equality.
The Healthy Lifetime Income indicator makes equality and corruption largely irrelevant for well-being.
An economy that strengthens health follows the same logic that ties well-being to life expectancy and care.
tactical_explanations:
Better life expectancy and care → higher well-being even with more moderate material prosperity. Health carries.

The statement is true.

Pure income growth is the weaker, not the stronger, long-term motor. Health, environment and stability weigh more.

The statement is false.

Similar GDP does not level happiness scores; inequality and corruption lower them. Equality keeps scores higher.

The statement is true.

Healthy Lifetime Income widens the view to health; equality and corruption remain relevant for happiness scores. Irrelevance would be false.

The statement is false.

Strengthening health means working on life expectancy and care — the same logic as with the indicator.

The statement is true.

title: Means, dimensions and the good life
context: Evaluate the following statements on the relation of means–ends logic and the three sustainability dimensions:
statements: Economic stability and ecological sustainability remain means to the freedom to lead a good life, even if the sustainable economy must integrate three dimensions.
The ecological dimension (staying within planetary boundaries) makes ecological sustainability an end in itself and erases the good life.
The social dimension (everyone's needs, less inequality) fits the evidence that high equality goes with high happiness scores and strong inequality depresses the scores.
The psychological dimension (subjective well-being and meaning) drops away as soon as stability and sustainability are only means.
Well-being arises where needs, ecological stability and social relationships come together, that is where the three dimensions practically take hold.
tactical_explanations:
Means–ends logic and three dimensions do not contradict each other: stability and sustainability serve the good life that is integrated socially, ecologically and psychologically.

The statement is true.

Ecological dimension means keeping limits as part of a sustainable economy, not an end in itself without the good life. The goal remains freedom to a good life.

The statement is false.

Social dimension and happiness evidence fit: high equality — high scores; strong inequality — lower scores. Theory and empirics interlock.

The statement is true.

As means, stability and sustainability remain oriented to the good life; the psychological dimension (SWB and meaning) therefore does not drop away but belongs.

The statement is false.

Needs, ecological stability, social relationships: there the three dimensions practically take hold and well-being arises.

The statement is true.

title: Traps around GDP, absolutes and ends in themselves
context: Evaluate the following statements on typical shortenings of the societal preconditions of well-being:
statements: Because well-being arises in a social context, trust, cooperation and equality suffice to explain environmental quality for life satisfaction as largely irrelevant.
Young people in participatory education systems report higher life satisfaction and lower future anxiety; this finding stands beside, not in place of, the environment and equality findings.
A sustainable economy can leave out the psychological dimension because economic stability is already an end in itself.
Intact ecosystems measurably raise life satisfaction while land sealing lowers it; both effects remain even if the GDP of two countries is similar.
Pure income growth without strengthening health, environmental quality and social stability is the surest path to lastingly higher happiness.
tactical_explanations:
Social factors and environmental quality do not exclude each other. Clean air and green spaces raise life satisfaction measurably; social factors do not replace them.

The statement is false.

Participatory education stands beside environment and equality findings, not in their place. Several societal preconditions act in parallel.

The statement is true.

Stability is a means, not an end in itself; the psychological dimension must not be left out. Three dimensions remain mandatory.

The statement is false.

Environmental effects on life satisfaction remain even with similar GDP. GDP does not level these effects.

The statement is true.

Pure income growth is the weaker long-term path. Health, environmental quality and social stability raise happiness more strongly.

The statement is false.
